1738.subject: Physics
1738.text: A bi-convex lens is formed with two thin plano-convex lenses as shown in the figure. Refractive index $n$ of the first lens is 1.5 and that of the second lens is 1.2. Both the curved surfaces are of the same radius of curvature $R=14 \mathrm{~cm}$. For this bi-convex lens, for an object distance of $40 \mathrm{~cm}$, the image distance will be
1738.sol:
According to lens maker's formula
$\frac{1}{f}=(n-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
For the first lens : $n=1.5, R_1=+14 \mathrm{~cm}, R_2=\infty$
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{f_1}=(1.5-1)\left(\frac{1}{14}-\frac{1}{\infty}\right)=\frac{0.5}{14}$
For the second lens : $n=1.2, R_1=\infty, R_2=-14 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\therefore \quad \frac{1}{f_2}=(1.2-1)\left(\frac{1}{\infty}-\frac{1}{-14}\right)=\frac{0.2}{14}$
The focal length of the bi-convex lens is
$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_2}=\frac{0.5}{14}+\frac{0.2}{14}=\frac{0.7}{14}=\frac{1}{20}$
According to thin lens formula; $\frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{1}{f}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{-40}=\frac{1}{20}$ or $v=40 \mathrm{~cm}$

5161.text: The density of nitric acid solution is $1.5 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mL}^{-1}$. Its weight percentage is 68 . What is the approximate concentration (in $\left.\mathrm{mol} \mathrm{L}^{-1}\right)$ of nitric acid? $(\mathrm{N}=14 u ; \mathrm{O}=16 u ; \mathrm{H}=1 u)$
5161.sol:
$\begin{aligned} & \text{ Given }- \text{ Density }(\delta)=1.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{ml} \\ & \text{ Volume }(\mathrm{v})=1000 \mathrm{ml} \\ & \text{ Weight percentage }=68 \\ & \text{ Mass of solution }=\text{ density } \times \text{ volume } \\ & 1.5 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{ml} \times 1000 \mathrm{ml}=1500 \mathrm{~g} \\ & \text{ Mass of Nitric Acid }=\text{ weight percentage } \times \text{ Total mass of } \\ & \text{ solution. }\end{aligned}$
Mass of Nitric acid $=0.68 \times 1500 \mathrm{~g}=1020 \mathrm{~g}$ Molar mass of Nitric Acid $\left(\mathrm{HNO}_2\right)=1(\mathrm{H})+14(\mathrm{~N})+3 \times 16(0)=63 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}$
Moles of Nitric acid $=\frac{\text{ mass }}{\text{ molar mass }}$
Moles of Nitric acid $=\frac{1020 \mathrm{~g}}{63 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol}}=16.19 \mathrm{~mol}\operatorname{Molarity}(\mathrm{m})=\frac{\text{ moles of solute }}{\text{ Volume of solution in litres }}$
Molarity $=\frac{16.19 \mathrm{~mol}}{\mathrm{LL}}=19.19 \mathrm{~m} \approx 16.2$

\end{aligned}
so equation of required circle is
\begin{aligned} \text{ and } \left( x-\frac{4}{5}\right)^2+\left( y-\frac{7}{5}\right)^2=(3)^2 \\
\Rightarrow & x²-\frac{8 x}{5}+\frac{16}{25}+ y^2-\frac{14 y}{5}+\frac{49}{25}=9 \\
\Rightarrow & x²+y²-\frac{8 x}{5}-\frac{14 y}{5}+\frac{65}{25}=9 \\
\Rightarrow & x²+y²-\frac{8 x}{5}-\frac{14 y}{5}+\frac{13}{5}=9 \\
\Rightarrow & 5 x²+5 y²-8 x-14 y-32=0

9524.text: For how many distinct values of $x$, the equation $sin\left[2\cos^{-1}cot\left(2\tan^{-1}x\right)\right] = 0$ holds?
9524.sol:
Given, $sin\left[2\cos^{-1}cot\left(2\tan^{-1}x\right)\right] = 0$

Let $\tan^{-1}x = y ⇒ x = tany$

Then, $sin\left[2\cos^{-1}cot\left(2y\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - \tan^{2}y}{2tany}\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[\cos^{-1}\left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ sin\left[\sin^{-1}\sqrt{1 - \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2}}\right] = 0$

$⇒ \sqrt{1 - \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ 1 - \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right)^{2} = 1$

$⇒ \left(2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} - 1\right) = \pm 1$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 1 \pm 1 = 2, 0$

$⇒ 2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 2$ or $2\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right)^{2} = 1$ or $1 - x^{2} = 0$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{1 - x^{2}}{2x}\right) = \pm 1$ or $x = \pm 1$

$⇒ x^{2} + 2x - 1 = 0, x^{2} - 2x - 1 = 0$ or $x = \pm 1$

$⇒ x = - 1 \pm \sqrt{2}, x = 1 \pm \sqrt{2}$ or $x = \pm 1$

Hence, there are $6$possible values of $x$.

12631.sol:
We have,
$3 l m-4 l n+m n=0\ldots$ (i)
and $l+2 m+3 n=0\ldots$ (ii)
From Eq. (ii), $l=-(2 m+3 n)$ Using in Eq. (i), we get
$-3(2 m+3 n) m+4(2 m+3 n) n+m n=0\Rightarrow \quad-6 m^2-9 m n+8 m n+12 n^2+m n=0\Rightarrow \quad-6 m^2+12 n^2=0$
Now, $m^2=2 n^2 \Rightarrow m= \pm \sqrt{2} n$
Now, $\quad m=\sqrt{2} n\Rightarrow \quad l=-(2 \sqrt{2} n+3 n)=-(2 \sqrt{2}+3) n\therefore l: m: n=-(3+2 \sqrt{2}) n: \sqrt{2} n: n=-(3+2 \sqrt{2}): \sqrt{2}: 1$
Also, $\quad m=-\sqrt{2} n \Rightarrow l=-(-2 \sqrt{2}+3) nl: m: n=-(3-2 \sqrt{2}) n:-\sqrt{2} n: n=-(3-2 \sqrt{2}):-\sqrt{2}: 1$
If $\theta$ is the angle between the lines, then
$\cos \theta=\frac{l_1 l_2+m_1 m_2+n_1 n_2}{\sqrt{l_1^2+m_1^2+n_1^2} \sqrt{l_2^2+m_2^2+n_2^2}}=\frac{(3+2 \sqrt{2})(3-2 \sqrt{2})+(\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2})+1.1}{\sqrt{(3+2 \sqrt{2})^2+(\sqrt{2})^2+1^2}{\sqrt{(3-2 \sqrt{2})^2+(-\sqrt{2})^2+1^2}}}=\frac{9-8-2+1}{\sqrt{9+8+12 \sqrt{2}+2+1} \sqrt{9+8-12 \sqrt{2}+2+1}}=0\Rightarrow \cos \theta=0 \Rightarrow \cos \theta=\cos \frac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$

15838.text: A body is projected at an angle $\theta$ so that its range is maximum. If $T$ is the time of flight, then the value of maximum range is (acceleration due to gravity $=g$ )

We know that,
Range of projectile R=$\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}$ As range is maximum, $\theta=45^{{}^{\circ}}$
R_{\max }=$\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \times 45}{g}=\frac{u^2}{g}$ Flight time of projectile, T=$\frac{2 u \sin 45^{{}^{\circ}}}{g} \begin{aligned}& =\frac{2 u}{\sqrt{2} \cdot g}=\frac{\sqrt{2} \cdot u}{g}\\
\text{ or } \quad u & =\frac{T g}{\sqrt{2}}
\end{aligned}$ or
Putting these value of $u$ in Eq. (i), we get $\begin{aligned}& R_{\max }=\frac{1}{g}\left(\frac{T g}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 \\
& R_{\max }=\frac{1}{2} g T²
\end{aligned}
$

Thus, compound [X] is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, which has the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$.

Dehydration of [X] with 20% $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4$ or heating with Cu at 573 K yields 2-methylpropene [Y].

$(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C-OH} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Tertiary alcohols do not undergo oxidation with PCC, hence [X] shows no reaction.

Vigorous oxidation of [X] with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ involves dehydration to [Y] followed by oxidative cleavage of the double bond to form acetone, $\text{CO}_2$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Therefore, [X] is 2-methylpropan-2-ol and [Y] is 2-methylpropene.

Answer: [X]: 2–Methylpropan–2–ol [Y]: 2–Methylpropene

20628.subject: Chemistry
20628.text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At 300 K , the vapour pressure of pure A and pure B are $8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{ Pa}$ and $12 \times 10^3 \mathrm{ Pa}$ respectively. If the solution has 40 mole percent of $A$, the composition of $A$ and $B$ in the vapour phase is:
20628.sol:
Given the mole fraction of A in the liquid phase $x_A = 0.40$.

Since the solution is ideal, the mole fraction of B in the liquid phase is $x_B = 1 - x_A = 1 - 0.40 = 0.60$.

The vapour pressures of pure components are $P_A^{0} = 8 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa}$ and $P_B^{0} = 12 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa}$.

The partial pressures of A and B in the vapour phase are given by Raoult's Law:
$P_A = x_A P_A^{0} = 0.40 \times 8 \times 10^3 = 3.2 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa}$
$P_B = x_B P_B^{0} = 0.60 \times 12 \times 10^3 = 7.2 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa}$

The total vapour pressure $P_{total} = P_A + P_B = 3.2 \times 10^3 + 7.2 \times 10^3 = 10.4 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa}$.

The mole fraction of A in the vapour phase $y_A$ is given by:
$y_A = \dfrac{P_A}{P_{total}} = \dfrac{3.2 \times 10^3}{10.4 \times 10^3} = \dfrac{3.2}{10.4} = \dfrac{32}{104} = \dfrac{4}{13} \approx 0.3077$.

The mole fraction of B in the vapour phase $y_B$ is given by:
$y_B = 1 - y_A = 1 - 0.3077 = 0.6923$.

Rounding to two decimal places, $y_A \approx 0.30$ and $y_B \approx 0.70$.

Answer: 0.30 and 0.70

20953.subject: Mathematics
20953.text: For a given curve $y=2 x-x^2$, when $x$ increases at the rate of 3 units/sec, then how does the slope of the curve change?
20953.sol:
The equation of the curve is given by $y = 2x - x^2$.

The slope of the curve at any point $x$ is given by $m = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2 - 2x$.

To find the rate of change of the slope with respect to time $t$, we differentiate $m$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dm}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(2 - 2x) = -2 \dfrac{dx}{dt}$.

Given that the rate of increase of $x$ is $\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 3$ units/sec, we substitute this value into the expression:

$\dfrac{dm}{dt} = -2 \times 3 = -6$ units/sec.

The negative sign indicates that the slope is decreasing at a rate of 6 units/sec.

Answer: Decreasing at 6 units/sec

21352.subject: Mathematics
21352.text: $The general solution of the differential equation \left(1+y^2\right) d x=\left(\tan ^{-1} y-x\right) d y$
21352.sol:
The given differential equation is $(1+y^2) dx = (\tan^{-1} y - x) dy$.

Rearranging the terms, we get $\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y - x}{1+y^2}$.

This can be written as $\dfrac{dx}{dy} + \dfrac{x}{1+y^2} = \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y}{1+y^2}$.

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dx}{dy} + P(y)x = Q(y)$, where $P(y) = \dfrac{1}{1+y^2}$ and $Q(y) = \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y}{1+y^2}$.

The integrating factor (IF) is $e^{\int P(y) dy} = e^{\int \dfrac{1}{1+y^2} dy} = e^{\tan^{-1} y}$.

The solution is given by $x \cdot IF = \int Q(y) \cdot IF dy + c$.

$x e^{\tan^{-1} y} = \int \dfrac{\tan^{-1} y}{1+y^2} e^{\tan^{-1} y} dy + c$.

Let $u = \tan^{-1} y$, then $du = \dfrac{1}{1+y^2} dy$.

The integral becomes $\int u e^u du = u e^u - \int e^u du = u e^u - e^u = e^u(u-1)$.

Substituting back, $x e^{\tan^{-1} y} = e^{\tan^{-1} y}(\tan^{-1} y - 1) + c$.

Dividing by $e^{\tan^{-1} y}$, we get $x = \tan^{-1} y - 1 + c e^{-\tan^{-1} y}$.

Answer: $x=\tan ^{-1} y-1+c e^{-\tan ^{-1} y}$

21994.subject: Mathematics
21994.text: The sum of four numbers in a geometric progression is 60 , and the arithmetic mean of the first and the last number is 18. Then the numbers are
21994.sol:
Let the four numbers in geometric progression be $a, ar, ar^2, ar^3$.

The sum of the four numbers is $a + ar + ar^2 + ar^3 = 60$.

This can be written as $a(1 + r + r^2 + r^3) = 60$, or $a(1 + r)(1 + r^2) = 60$.

The arithmetic mean of the first and last number is $\dfrac{a + ar^3}{2} = 18$, which implies $a(1 + r^3) = 36$.

Since $1 + r^3 = (1 + r)(1 - r + r^2)$, we have $a(1 + r)(1 - r + r^2) = 36$.

Dividing the two equations: $\dfrac{a(1 + r)(1 + r^2)}{a(1 + r)(1 - r + r^2)} = \dfrac{60}{36} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

This simplifies to $\dfrac{1 + r^2}{1 - r + r^2} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Cross-multiplying gives $3 + 3r^2 = 5 - 5r + 5r^2$, which rearranges to $2r^2 - 5r + 2 = 0$.

Factoring the quadratic: $(2r - 1)(r - 2) = 0$, so $r = 2$ or $r = 1/2$.

If $r = 2$, $a(1 + 2^3) = 36 \Rightarrow 9a = 36 \Rightarrow a = 4$. The numbers are $4, 8, 16, 32$.

If $r = 1/2$, $a(1 + (1/2)^3) = 36 \Rightarrow a(9/8) = 36 \Rightarrow a = 32$. The numbers are $32, 16, 8, 4$.

Comparing with the given options, $4, 8, 16, 32$ is present.

Answer: $4,8,16,32$

23668.subject: Physics
23668.text: In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width is found to be $0.4 \mathrm{ mm}$. If the whole apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\dfrac{4}{3}$ without changing geometrical arrangement, the new fringe width will be
23668.sol:
The fringe width $\beta$ in Young's double slit experiment is given by the formula $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light, $D$ is the distance between the slits and the screen, and $d$ is the distance between the two slits.

When the apparatus is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\mu$, the wavelength of light changes to $\lambda' = \dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}$.

The new fringe width $\beta'$ becomes $\beta' = \dfrac{\lambda' D}{d} = \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d} = \dfrac{\beta}{\mu}$.

Given $\beta = 0.4 \text{ mm}$ and $\mu = \dfrac{4}{3}$, we calculate the new fringe width as $\beta' = \dfrac{0.4}{4/3} = 0.4 \times \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.3 \text{ mm}$.

Answer: 0.30 mm

We shall consider 3 cases.

Case I: When p = 0

Case II: When circle intersect x-axis at 2 distinct points and touches y-axis.

${g}^{2} - c > 0$ and ${f}^{2} = c$

25319.text: The locus of the mid-point of the chord of contact of tangents drawn from points lying on the straight line $4 x-$ $5 y=20$ to the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=9$ is
25319.sol:
Any point $P$ on line $4 x-5 y=20$ can be considered as $\left(\alpha, \frac{4 \alpha-20}{5}\right)$. Equation of chord of contact $A B$ to the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=9$ drawn from point $\mathrm{P}\left(\alpha, \frac{4 \alpha-20}{5}\right)$ is x. $\alpha+$ y. $\left(\frac{4 \alpha-20}{5}\right)=9...(i)$
Also the equation of chord $A B$ whose mid point is $(h, k)$ is $h x+k y=h^{2}+k^{2}....(ii)$ $\because \quad$ Equations (i) and (ii) represent the same line, $\therefore \quad \frac{h}{\alpha}=\frac{k}{\frac{4 \alpha-20}{5}}=\frac{h^{2}+k^{2}}{9}$ $\Rightarrow 5 k \alpha=4 h \alpha-20 h$ and $9 h=\alpha\left(h^{2}+k^{2}\right)$ $\Rightarrow \alpha=\frac{20 h}{4 h-5 k} \quad$ and $\alpha=\frac{9 h}{h^{2}+k^{2}}$ $\Rightarrow \quad \frac{20 h}{4 h-5 k}=\frac{9 h}{h^{2}+k^{2}} \Rightarrow 20\left(h^{2}+k^{2}\right)=9(4 h-5 k)$ $\therefore \quad$ Locus of $(h, k)$ is $20\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)-36 x+45 y=0$

27183.subject: Chemistry
27183.text:
Which statements are True?
A. In Hoffmann bromamide degradation, $4$ moles of NaOH and $2$ moles of Br$_2$ are consumed per mole of an amide
B. Hoffmann bromamide reaction is not given by alkyl amides.
C. Primary amines can be synthesized by Hoffmann bromamide degradation.
D. Secondary amide on reaction with Br$_2$ and NaOH will give secondary amine.
E. The by-products of Hoffmann degradation are Na$_2$CO$_3$, NaBr and H$_2$O.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
27183.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for Hoffmann bromamide degradation is:

$\text{R-CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{R-NH}_2 + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{NaBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Statement A is false because $1$ mole of $\text{Br}_2$ and $4$ moles of $\text{NaOH}$ are consumed per mole of amide.

Statement B is false because primary alkyl amides readily undergo this reaction.

Statement C is true as the primary product of this reaction is a primary amine.

Statement D is false because the reaction is strictly given by primary amides ($\text{R-CONH}_2$), not secondary amides.

Statement E is true as the by-products formed are $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, $\text{NaBr}$, and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Therefore, only statements C and E are true.

Answer: C and E only

28479.subject: Chemistry
28479.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
28479.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is $\mathrm{Al}>\mathrm{Mg}>\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}>\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$.
Statement II : The correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is $\mathrm{Cl}>\mathrm{Br}>\mathrm{S}>\mathrm{O}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
28479.sol:
Analyzing Statement I: The order given is Al > Mg > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺. However, the correct atomic radii order should be Mg > Al because Mg is in group 2 (period 3) while Al is in group 13 (period 3), and moving right across a period decreases radius. The correct order would be Mg > Al > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺. Therefore, Statement I is FALSE.

Analyzing Statement II: Electron gain enthalpy magnitudes follow: Cl (highest, ~349 kJ/mol) > Br (~325) > S (~200) > O (~141). This is because Cl has the highest tendency to gain an electron due to its position and electronic configuration. Statement II is TRUE.

Since Statement I is false and Statement II is true, the answer is option (3).

30736.subject: Chemistry
30736.text: The solubility product constants of $Ag_2CrO_4 and AgBr$ are $32x and 4y$ respectively at $298$ K. The value of $\left(\dfrac{\text{molarity of } Ag_2CrO_4}{\text{molarity of } AgBr}\right)$ can be expressed as :
30736.sol:
Let the solubility of $Ag_2CrO_4$ be $S_1$.

For $Ag_2CrO_4 \rightleftharpoons 2Ag^+ + CrO_4^{2-}$

$K_{sp} = (2S_1)^2(S_1) = 4S_1^3$

$4S_1^3 = 32x \Rightarrow S_1^3 = 8x \Rightarrow S_1 = 2\sqrt[3]{x}$

Let the solubility of $AgBr$ be $S_2$.

For $AgBr \rightleftharpoons Ag^+ + Br^-$

$K_{sp} = S_2^2$

$S_2^2 = 4y \Rightarrow S_2 = 2\sqrt{y}$

The ratio of their molarities is:

$\dfrac{S_1}{S_2} = \dfrac{2\sqrt[3]{x}}{2\sqrt{y}} = \dfrac{\sqrt[3]{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt[3]{x}}{\sqrt{y}}$

30977.subject: Chemistry
30977.text:
Find the correct statements related to group 15 hydrides.
A. Reducing nature increases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$
B. Tendency to donate lone pair of electrons decreases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$
C. The stability of hydrides decreases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$
D. HEH bond angle decreases from NH$_3$ to SbH$_3$ (E = Elements of group 15)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
30977.sol:
Statement A: The reducing nature of group 15 hydrides depends on the E-H bond strength. As the size of the central atom increases down the group, the E-H bond dissociation enthalpy decreases. Hence, the reducing character increases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$. This statement is correct.

Statement B: The basic character or the tendency to donate a lone pair of electrons depends on the electron density on the central atom. As the size of the central atom increases down the group, the electron density decreases. Thus, the basicity decreases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$. This statement is correct.

Statement C: Due to the decrease in E-H bond dissociation enthalpy down the group, the thermal stability of the hydrides decreases from NH$_3$ to BiH$_3$. This statement is correct.

Statement D: The H-E-H bond angle decreases down the group because the electronegativity of the central atom decreases and the size increases, causing the bond pairs to move further away from the central atom. This decreases the bond pair-bond pair repulsion. The bond angles are NH$_3$ ($107.8^{\circ}$), PH$_3$ ($93.6^{\circ}$), AsH$_3$ ($91.8^{\circ}$), and SbH$_3$ ($91.3^{\circ}$). This statement is correct.

All statements A, B, C, and D are correct.

Answer: A, B, C and D

33080.text: Let $\mathrm{A}_{1}$ be the bounded area enclosed by the curves $y=x^{2}+2, x+y=8$ and $y$-axis that lies in the first quadrant. Let $\mathrm{A}_{2}$ be the bounded area enclosed by the curves $y=x^{2}+2, y^{2}=x, x=2$, and $y$-axis that lies in the first quadrant. Then $\mathrm{A}_{1}-\mathrm{A}_{2}$ is equal to
33080.sol:
For $A_1$: intersection of $y = x^2 + 2$ and $x + y = 8$ at $x = 2, y = 6$
$A_1 = \int_0^2 (8-x-(x^2+2)) dx = \int_0^2 (6-x-x^2) dx = \left[6x - \frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2 = 12 - 2 - \frac{8}{3} = \frac{22}{3}$
For $A_2$: bounded by $y = x^2 + 2$, $y^2 = x$ (i.e., $x = y^2$), $x = 2$, and $y$-axis.
In first quadrant, $y^2 = x$ goes from (0,0) to (2,$\sqrt{2}$).
The parabola $y = x^2 + 2$ passes through (0,2) and (2,6).
$A_2 = \int_0^{\sqrt{2}} (2 - y^2) dy = \left[2y - \frac{y^3}{3}\right]_0^{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2} - \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$
$A_1 - A_2 = \frac{22}{3} - \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} = \frac{2}{3}(2\sqrt{2}+1)$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + \dfrac{3}{2} \times 2\mathop{\mathop{{\left[tan\dfrac{x}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{2}}$

$⇒ I = \mathop{\mathop{{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx}_{⏟}}_{{I}_{1}} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

Now solving ${I}_{1}$ we get,

${I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{2sinx}{\sin^{2}x\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{1}{sinx\left(1 + cosx\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 2{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{1}{\left(\dfrac{2tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{1 - tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}\right)}dx$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{∫}_{\dfrac{\pi}{3}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{\left[1 + \tan^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)}dx$

Put $tan\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right) = v ⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}{sec}^{2}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)dx = dv$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {∫}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}\dfrac{\left(1 + {v}^{2}\right)dv}{v}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\left[{\log}_{e}\left(v\right) + \dfrac{{v}^{2}}{2}\right]}_{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}^{1}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(1\right) - {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = {\log}_{e}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \dfrac{1}{3}$

So,

$I = \dfrac{1}{3} + {\log}_{e}\sqrt{3} + 3\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{10}{3} - \sqrt{3} + {\log}_{e}\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ v + y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = - \left({v}^{2} - v + 1\right)$

$⇒ y\dfrac{dv}{dy} = - {v}^{2} - 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{- dv}{1 + {v}^{2}} = \dfrac{dy}{y}$

Now Integrating Both side

$⇒ - ∫ \dfrac{dy}{1 + {v}^{2}} = ∫ \dfrac{dy}{y}$

$⇒ - \tan^{- 1}v = log\left|y\right| + c$ $⇒ - \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = log\left|y\right| + c$

Also this curve passes through $\left(1, 1\right)$

$⇒ \tan^{- 1}1 = log\left|1\right| + c$ $⇒ c = - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Now putting $y = \sqrt{3}x$ and $x = \alpha$ we get

$= - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}x} = log\left|\sqrt{3}\alpha\right| - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ $= - \tan^{- 1}\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = log\left(\sqrt{3}\alpha\right) - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$⇒ log\left|\sqrt{3}\alpha\right| = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$

35369.text: Let O be the origin, and P and Q be two points on the rectangular hyperbola $xy = 12$ such that the mid point of the line segment PQ is $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, -\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$. Then the area of the triangle OPQ equals:
35369.sol:
The equation of the chord of the hyperbola $xy = 12$ with midpoint $(x_1, y_1)$ is given by $T = S_1$.

$\dfrac{x y_1 + y x_1}{2} - 12 = x_1 y_1 - 12$

$x y_1 + y x_1 = 2 x_1 y_1$

Substituting the midpoint $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, -\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$:

$x\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + y\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$-x + y = -1 \Rightarrow y = x - 1$

To find the coordinates of P and Q, substitute $y = x - 1$ into the equation of the hyperbola $xy = 12$:

$x(x - 1) = 12$

$x^2 - x - 12 = 0$

$(x - 4)(x + 3) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 4, -3$

For $x = 4$, $y = 3$.

For $x = -3$, $y = -4$.

Thus, the coordinates of P and Q are $(4, 3)$ and $(-3, -4)$.

The area of triangle OPQ with vertices $(0,0)$, $(4,3)$, and $(-3,-4)$ is:

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} |x_P y_Q - x_Q y_P|$

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} |(4)(-4) - (-3)(3)|$

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} |-16 + 9| = \dfrac{7}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7}{2}$

If $\int \frac{x+1}{\sqrt{2 x-1}} \mathrm{~d} x=f(x) \sqrt{2 x-1}+\mathrm{C},$ where $\mathrm{C}$ is a constant

Put $\sqrt{2 x-1}=t$

$\begin{array}{l}

I=\int \frac{\left(t^{2}+3\right)}{2} d t=\frac{t^{3}}{6}+\frac{3 t}{2}+C \\

=\frac{(2 x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}}{6}+\frac{3}{2}(2 x-1)^{\frac{1}{2}}+C \\

=\sqrt{2 x-1}\left(\frac{x+4}{3}\right)+C \\

=f(x) \cdot \sqrt{2 x-1}+C

35881.subject: Mathematics
35881.text: If the Boolean expression $( p ∧ q ) ⊛ ( p ⊗ q )$ is a tautology, then $⊛$ and $⊗$ are respectively given by
35881.sol:
Option $\left(A\right)$

$( p ∧ q ) \to ( p \to q )$

We know that $a \to b = ~ a ∨ b$

$= ( p ∧ q ) ⟶ ( ~ p ∨ q )$

$= ~ ( p ∧ q ) ∨ ( ~ p ∨ q )$

Using De Morgan's Law i.e. $~ \left(a ∧ b\right) = ~ a ∨ ~ b,$

$= ( ~ p ∨ ~ q ) ∨ ( ~ p ∨ q )$

Using associative law and commutative law i.e. $\left(a ∨ b\right) ∨ c = a ∨ \left(b ∨ c\right) \text{ and } a ∨ b = b ∨ a,$

$= ~ p ∨ ( ~ q ∨ q )$

$= ~ p ∨ t$

$= t$

Option $( B )$

$( p ∧ q ) ∧ ( p ∨ q ) = ( p ∧ q )$

Which is not a tautology.

Option $( C )$

$( p ∧ q ) ∨ ( p \to q )$

$= ( p ∧ q ) ∨ ( ~ p ∨ q )$

$= ~ p ∨ q$

Which is not a tautology.

Option $( D )$

$( p ∧ q ) ∧ ( p \to q )$

$= ( p ∧ q ) ∧ ( ~ p ∨ q )$

$= p ∧ q$

Which is not a tautology.

Hence, the correct answer is option $\left(A\right) .

$

$∵ {7}^{n} = ( 10 - 3{)}^{n} = 10k + ( - 3{)}^{n}$

39091.subject: Physics
39091.text: A parallel plate capacitor is having separation between plates $0.885$ mm. It has a capacitance of $1\,\mu$F when the space between the plates is filled with an insulating material of resistivity $1\times 10^{13}\,\Omega$m and resistance $17.7\times 10^{14}\,\Omega$. Relative permittivity of the insulating material is $\alpha\times 10^7$. The value of $\alpha$ is ________. (Take permittivity of free space $=8.85\times 10^{-12}$ F/m)
39091.sol:
The resistance of the insulating material is given by $R = \dfrac{\rho d}{A}$.

The capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor is given by $C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 \epsilon_r A}{d}$.

Multiplying the expressions for $R$ and $C$, we get:

$RC = \rho \epsilon_0 \epsilon_r$

Rearranging for relative permittivity $\epsilon_r$:

$\epsilon_r = \dfrac{RC}{\rho \epsilon_0}$

Substituting the given values:

$\epsilon_r = \dfrac{17.7 \times 10^{14} \times 10^{-6}}{10^{13} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}$

$\epsilon_r = \dfrac{17.7 \times 10^8}{8.85 \times 10^1}$

$\epsilon_r = 2 \times 10^7$

Comparing this with the given expression $\epsilon_r = \alpha \times 10^7$, we get:

$\alpha = 2$

Answer: $2$

39670.subject: Physics
39670.text: In a potentiometer arrangement, a cell of emf $1 . 20V$ gives a balance point at $36cm$ length of wire. This cell is now replaced by another cell of emf $1 . 80V$. The difference in balancing length of potentiometer wire in above conditions will be _____ $cm$.
39670.sol:
In a potentiometer, null point or balance point is defined as the point where the deflection of the galvanometer is zero. If emf of the unknown battery is $ε$ then,

$ε =$(Potential Gradient)$\times$(Balancing length $l$). Therefore,

$\dfrac{{ε}_{1}}{{ε}_{2}} = \dfrac{{l}_{1}}{{l}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 . 20}{1 . 80} = \dfrac{36}{{l}_{2}}$

$⇒ {l}_{2} = 18 \times 3 = 54cm$

Hence, difference in balancing length is ${l}_{2} - {l}_{1} = 54 - 36 = 18cm$

41256.subject: Physics
41256.text: The time taken by an object to slide down $45 °$ rough inclined plane is $n$ times as it takes to slide down a perfectly smooth $45 °$ incline plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the incline plane is:
41256.sol:
Let angle of inclination is $\theta = 45 °$.

Then, acceleration along the incline in case of smooth incline will be, ${a}_{1} = gsin\theta = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}$.

In case of rough incline, kinetic friction will act against the direction of motion. Normal force acting on the object will be $mgcos\theta$. Therefore, acceleration along the incline in case of rough incline will be,

${a}_{2} = gsin\theta - \mugcos\theta = \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{\mug}{\sqrt{2}}$.

Now as per question,

${t}_{2} = n{t}_{1}$

and as the displacement covered is the same in both case, $0 + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{1}{t}_{1}^{2} = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}{a}_{2}{t}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}{t}_{1}^{2} = \left(\dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}} - \dfrac{\mug}{\sqrt{2}}\right){n}^{2}{t}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ \mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{{n}^{2}}$

42872.subject: Physics
42872.text: Consider light travelling from a medium $A$ to medium $B$ separated by a plane interface. If the light undergoes total internal reflection during its travel from medium $A$ to $B$ and the speed of light in media $A$ and $B$ are $2.4 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $2.7 \times 10^{8} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, respectively, then the value of critical angle is :
42872.sol:
The refractive index of a medium is inversely proportional to the speed of light in that medium, given by $n = \frac{c}{v}$.
For light travelling from medium $A$ to medium $B$, the critical angle $\theta_c$ is defined when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium.
Given speeds are $v_A = 2.4 \times 10^8$ m/s and $v_B = 2.7 \times 10^8$ m/s.
The refractive indices are $n_A = \frac{c}{v_A}$ and $n_B = \frac{c}{v_B}$.
The critical angle $\theta_c$ is given by $\sin \theta_c = \frac{n_B}{n_A} = \frac{v_A}{v_B}$.
Substituting the values: $\sin \theta_c = \frac{2.4 \times 10^8}{2.7 \times 10^8} = \frac{24}{27} = \frac{8}{9}$.
To find the value in terms of $\tan^{-1}$, we use the trigonometric identity for a right-angled triangle where perpendicular $p = 8$ and hypotenuse $h = 9$.
The base $b = \sqrt{h^2 - p^2} = \sqrt{9^2 - 8^2} = \sqrt{81 - 64} = \sqrt{17}$.
Thus, $\tan \theta_c = \frac{p}{b} = \frac{8}{\sqrt{17}}$.
Therefore, $\theta_c = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{\sqrt{17}}\right)$.

49466.text: If $n(A) = 2$ and the number of relations from set A to set B is $1024$, then $n(B)$ is
49466.sol:
Let $n(A) = p$ and $n(B) = q$.

The number of relations from set A to set B is given by $2^{p \times q}$.

Given $n(A) = 2$, we have $p = 2$.

The number of relations is $1024$, so $2^{2q} = 1024$.

Since $1024 = 2^{10}$, we get $2^{2q} = 2^{10}$.

Equating the exponents, $2q = 10 \Rightarrow q = 5$.

Therefore, $n(B) = 5$.

Answer: $5$

55753.subject: Chemistry
55753.text: What is the number of bond pair of electrons and lone pair of electrons present in the valence shell of chalcogens in their hydride ?
options: 2 - Bond pair and 1- lone pair of electrons
2 - Bond pair and 2- lone pair of electrons
3 - Bond pair and 1- lone pair of electrons
3 - Bond pair and 2- lone pair of electrons
55753.sol:
Chalcogens belong to Group 16 of the periodic table and have 6 valence electrons (ns^2 np^4$).

The general formula for the hydrides of chalcogens is $H_2E$ (where $E = O, S, Se, Te, Po$).

In the formation of $H_2E$, the chalcogen atom shares two of its valence electrons with two hydrogen atoms to form two single covalent bonds. This results in 2 bond pairs of electrons.

The remaining 4 valence electrons on the chalcogen atom do not participate in bonding and exist as 2 lone pairs of electrons.

Thus, the valence shell of a chalcogen in its hydride contains 2 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs of electrons.$

56455.text: $What type of hybridisation is present in square planar geometry of complex \left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_4\right]^{2-}$
56455.sol:
Oxidation state of nickel: With CN^{-} ligands (charge -1) and overall charge -2, $x + 4(-1) = -2$ yields $x = +2$, so Ni^{2+} is present.

Electron configuration: Ni atom is [Ar] 4s^{2} 3d^{8}, so Ni^{2+} is [Ar] 3d^{8}.

Effect of ligand field: Cyanide is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of electrons in d-orbitals.

The d^{8} configuration with pairing renders one 3d orbital empty. Hybridization involves this empty d orbital, the empty 4s orbital, and two empty 4p orbitals, forming $ sp^2d$ hybridization.

This hybridization is consistent with the square planar geometry of the complex. The answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

57183.text: What is IUPAC name of the following compound?
57183.sol:
IUPAC nomenclature follows priority rules where aldehyde and carboxylic acid groups both take precedence, but benzaldehyde derivatives permit common naming conventions.

The compound contains aldehyde, carboxylic acid, and methyl substituents on a benzene ring. While carboxylic acid holds higher priority, benzaldehyde serves as an acceptable parent name when it yields clearer nomenclature. Numbering begins at the aldehyde carbon (C-1), placing carboxylic acid ortho at C-2 and methyl para at C-4.

Substituents are listed alphabetically: carboxy precedes methyl. The systematic name becomes 2-carboxy-4-methylbenzaldehyde.

Among the options, this corresponds to choice A.

57598.subject: Chemistry
57598.text: Identify the product when chlorobenzene is heated with nitrating mixture.
57598.sol:
Nitration of chlorobenzene proceeds via electrophilic aromatic substitution with the nitronium ion $\mathrm{NO_2+}$.

The chloro substituent exhibits both inductive electron-withdrawing and mesomeric electron-donating effects, rendering it ortho-para directing while deactivating the ring. Attack occurs at both ortho and para positions relative to chlorine.

This yields two isomeric products: 1-chloro-2-nitrobenzene and 1-chloro-4-nitrobenzene.

The para isomer predominates due to reduced steric hindrance compared to the ortho position.

57612.subject: Chemistry
57612.text: Which of the following is NOT obtained when a mixture of chloroethane and 1-chloropropane is treated with sodium metal in dry ether?
57612.sol:
The Wurtz reaction couples alkyl halides with sodium metal in dry ether to form alkanes. With chloroethane and 1-chloropropane, three products form via self-coupling and cross-coupling.

Let $R_1 = CH_3CH_2$– (ethyl) and $R_2 = CH_3CH_2CH_2$– (propyl). Self-coupling of chloroethane yields butane (C_4H_{10}$):
$R_1R_1 = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3$.

Self-coupling of 1-chloropropane yields hexane (C_6H_{14}$):
$R_2R_2 = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3$.

Cross-coupling yields pentane (C_5H_{12}$):
$R_1R_2 = CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2CH_3$.

Propane (C_3H_8$) is not formed, as it lacks a coupling pathway. The correct option is A.

Hence the order of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{X}$ bond strength in $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{X}$ is, $\mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{ F} > \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{Cl} > \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{Br} > \mathrm{CH}_{3} \mathrm{I}$.

58040.subject: Chemistry
58040.text: $What is the pH of buffer solution prepared by mixing 0.01 M weak acid and 0.02 M salt of weak acid with strong base ?  \left(\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}=4 \cdot 680\right)$
58040.sol:
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for an acidic buffer is given by:

$\mathrm{pH} = \mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}} + \log \left( \frac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)

Given $[$\text{Acid}] =0.01\ \text{M}, $[$\text{Salt}] =0.02\ \text{M}, and \mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}} =4.680$:

$\mathrm{pH} = 4.680 + \log \left( \frac{0.02}{0.01} \right) =4.680 + \log 2$

Since $\log 2 \approx0.301$:

$\mathrm{pH} =4.680 + 0.301 = 4.981$

The options are A) 4.379, B) 2.379, C) 4.981, D) 2.981, so the correct choice is $\boxed{\text{C}}$.

58847.text: Calculate the edge length of bcc unit cell if radius of a particle present in it is 186 pm.
58847.sol:
For a body-centered cubic (BCC) unit cell, atoms contact along the body diagonal, establishing the geometric relationship $4r = \sqrt{3}a$, where $r$ is the atomic radius and $a$ is the edge length.

This yields $a = \frac{4r}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Given $r = 186 \times 10^{-10}$ cm, substitution gives:

$a = \frac{4 \times (186 \times 10^{-10})}{\sqrt{3}} \approx 429.559 \times 10^{-10}$ cm $\approx 4.296 \times 10^{-8}$ cm.

This value corresponds to option A.

60260.text: A particle moves along a curve $y=\frac{2 x^3-1}{3}$. The points on the curve at which the $y$ co-ordinate is changing 18 times the $x$ co-ordinate are
60260.sol:
The curve is described by $y = \frac{2x^3 - 1}{3}$, with the condition that $\frac{dy}{dt} = 18\frac{dx}{dt}$.

Differentiating implicitly with respect to $t$ gives $\frac{dy}{dt} = 2x^2\frac{dx}{dt}$.

Equating the two expressions for $\frac{dy}{dt}$ yields $18\frac{dx}{dt} = 2x^2\frac{dx}{dt}$. Since $\frac{dx}{dt} \neq 0$, this simplifies to $18 = 2x^2 or x^2 = 9$, giving $x = \pm 3$.

Substituting into the original equation: at $x = 3$, $y = \frac{2(27) - 1}{3} = \frac{53}{3}$; at $x = -3$, $y = \frac{2(-27) - 1}{3} = -\frac{55}{3}$.

The corresponding points are $\left(3, \frac{53}{3}\right)$ and $\left(-3, -\frac{55}{3}\right)$, which correspond to option D.

61658.subject: Mathematics
61658.text: If $\cot[f(x)] = \dfrac{3x - x^3}{1 - 3x^2}$ and $\sin[g(x)] = \dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}$, then $\lim\limits_{x \to t}\dfrac{f(x) - f(t)}{g(x) - g(t)} = \ldots$
61658.sol:
Given $\cot[f(x)] = \dfrac{3x - x^3}{1 - 3x^2}$

Substituting $x = \tan\theta$, we get:

$\cot[f(x)] = \dfrac{3\tan\theta - \tan^3\theta}{1 - 3\tan^2\theta} = \tan(3\theta)$

$\cot[f(x)] = \cot \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} -$3$\theta\right)

$\Rightarrow f(x) = $\dfrac{\pi}{2} -$3$\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} -$3\tan^{-1}x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = $\dfrac{-3}{1 + x^2}

Similarly, given $\sin[g(x)] = $\dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}

Substituting $x = \tan$\theta, we get:

$\sin[g(x)] = $\dfrac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta} = \cos($2$\theta)

$\sin[g(x)] = \sin $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\theta\right)$

$\Rightarrow g(x) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\tan^{-1}x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$g'(x) = \dfrac{-2}{1 + x^2}$

The given limit is in the form of the definition of the derivative (or can be evaluated using L'Hospital's Rule):

$\lim\limits_{x \to t}\dfrac{f(x) - f(t)}{g(x) - g(t)} = \dfrac{f'(t)}{g'(t)}$

Substituting the derivatives at $x = t$:

$\dfrac{f'(t)}{g'(t)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{-3}{1 + t^2}}{\dfrac{-2}{1 + t^2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}$

62921.text: If p, q, r are simple propositions with truth values T, F, T respectively, then which of the following is not a true statement?
62921.sol:
Given $p = T$, $q = F$, $r = T$.

Evaluating the first option:
$[q \wedge (p \to q)] \to p \equiv [F \wedge (T \to F)] \to T \equiv [F \wedge F] \to T \equiv F \to T \equiv T$

Evaluating the second option:
$(p \wedge q) \to (q \vee \sim p) \equiv (T \wedge F) \to (F \vee F) \equiv F \to F \equiv T$

Evaluating the third option:
$[(\sim p \vee q) \wedge \sim r] \leftrightarrow p \equiv [(F \vee F) \wedge F] \leftrightarrow T \equiv [F \wedge F] \leftrightarrow T \equiv F \leftrightarrow T \equiv F$

Evaluating the fourth option:
$(p \wedge q) \vee (\sim q \vee r) \equiv (T \wedge F) \vee (T \vee T) \equiv F \vee T \equiv T$

The statement in the third option is not true.

Answer: $[(\sim p \vee q) \wedge \sim r] \leftrightarrow p$

62934.subject: Mathematics
62934.text:
Which of the following statements is/are False?
$S_1 : \exists\, n \in \mathbb{N}$, such that $n^2 + n + 2$ is divisible by 4.
$S_2 : \exists\, x \in \mathbb{N}$, such that $x - 17 < 20$.
$S_3 : \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}, \quad x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0$.
$S_4 : \forall\, n \in \mathbb{N}, \quad n^2 \geq 1$.
62934.sol:
For $S_1$: Let $n = 1 \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $n^2 + n + 2 = 1^2 + 1 + 2 = 4$, which is divisible by $4$. Thus, there exists at least one natural number satisfying the condition, making $S_1$ true.

For $S_2$: Let $x = 1 \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $x - 17 = 1 - 17 = -16$, which is strictly less than $20$. Thus, there exists at least one natural number satisfying the condition, making $S_2$ true.

For $S_3$: The statement asserts that for all natural numbers, the equation $x^2 + 3x - 10 = 0$ holds. However, $x^2 + 3x - 10 = (x + 5)(x - 2) = 0$ is only satisfied for $x = 2$ and $x = -5$. It does not hold for all natural numbers (for example, $x = 1$ gives $-6 \neq 0$). Thus, $S_3$ is false.

For $S_4$: The set of natural numbers is $N = \{1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we have $n \geq 1$, which implies $n^2 \geq 1$. Thus, $S_4$ is true.

Therefore, only statement $S_3$ is false.

Answer: Only $S_3$.

65576.text: Alternating current of peak value $\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)$ A flows through the primary coil of a transformer. The coefficient of mutual inductance between primary and secondary coils is $1$ H. The peak em.f. induced in secondary coil is (Frequency of a. c. is $50$ Hz)
65576.sol:
The alternating current in the primary coil is given by $I_p = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$, where $I_0$ is the peak current and $\omega = 2\pi f$.

The induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is given by Faraday's law of induction:

$e_s = -M \dfrac{dI_p}{dt}$

$e_s = -M \dfrac{d}{dt} (I_0 \sin(\omega t))$

$e_s = -M I_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)$

The peak e.m.f. induced in the secondary coil is the maximum value of $e_s$, which is:

$E_0 = M I_0 \omega$

Given values are:

$M = 1$ H

$I_0 = \dfrac{2}{\pi}$ A

$f = 50$ Hz $\Rightarrow \omega = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi$ rad/s

Substituting these values into the equation for peak e.m.f.:

$E_0 = 1 \times \left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right) \times 100\pi$

$E_0 = 200$ V

Answer: $200$ V

$k = \frac{1.08}{2.16} = 0.5\text{ V/m}$

$2.5 = 0.5L$

$L = \frac{2.5}{0.5} = 5\text{ m}$

The potentiometer wire length is $\boxed{\text{C}}$

66341.text: In the following circuit, the current through $6 \Omega$ resistor is
66341.sol:
Parallel branch simplification: With identical $3\text{ V}$ sources and $3\ \Omega$ resistors in parallel, the Norton equivalent conductance is $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$ S, so equivalent resistance is $R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{3}{2}\ \Omega$.

Equivalent current source is $\frac{3\text{ V}}{3\ \Omega} + \frac{3\text{ V}}{3\ \Omega} = 2\text{ A}$, yielding $V_{\text{eq}} = 2\text{ A} \times \frac{3}{2}\ \Omega = 3\text{ V}$.

Total circuit analysis: The $6\ \Omega$ resistor is in series with the $\frac{3}{2}\ \Omega$ equivalent resistance, giving total resistance $7.5\ \Omega$.

By Ohm's law, current is $I = \frac{3\text{ V}}{7.5\ \Omega} = \frac{2}{5}\text{ A}$.

Final current: $\boxed{\frac{2}{5}\text{ A}}$

68597.text: Activity of a radioactive sample decreases to $\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{th}$ of its original value in 4 days. Then in 16 days its activity will become $x$ times the original value. The value of $x$ is
68597.sol:
Let the initial activity be $A_0$ and the half-life be $T_{1/2}$.

The activity after time $t$ is given by $A = A_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}}}$.

Given that $A = \dfrac{A_0}{4}$ at $t = 4$ days:

$\dfrac{A_0}{4} = A_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{4}{T_{1/2}}}$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{4}{T_{1/2}}}$

$\dfrac{4}{T_{1/2}} = 2 \Rightarrow T_{1/2} = 2$ days.

After $t = 16$ days, the activity $A'$ is:

$A' = A_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\dfrac{16}{2}} = A_0 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^8 = \dfrac{A_0}{256}$

Thus, the activity becomes $\dfrac{1}{256}$ times the original value, so $x = \dfrac{1}{256}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{256}$

68601.subject: Physics
68601.text: The activity of a radioactive sample is measured as $N_0$ counts per minute at time $t = 0$ and $\dfrac{N_0}{e}$ counts per minute at time $t = 3$ minute. The time (in minute) in which the activity reduces to half the value, is
68601.sol:
The activity of a radioactive sample at time $t$ is given by $A = A_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.

Given that at $t = 0$, $A = N_0$.

At $t = 3$ minutes, $A = \dfrac{N_0}{e}$.

Substituting these values into the decay equation:

$\dfrac{N_0}{e} = N_0 e^{-3\lambda}$

$e^{-1} = e^{-3\lambda}$

Comparing the powers of $e$, we get:

$3\lambda = 1 \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{1}{3} \text{ min}^{-1}$

The time in which the activity reduces to half its initial value is the half-life $T_{1/2}$, which is given by:

$T_{1/2} = \dfrac{\log_e 2}{\lambda}$

Substituting the value of $\lambda$:

$T_{1/2} = \dfrac{\log_e 2}{\dfrac{1}{3}} = 3 \log_e 2 \text{ min}$

Answer: $3\log_e 2$

69447.subject: Physics
69447.text: Which of the following figure represents forward bias diode?
69447.sol:
A diode is forward-biased if the anode potential exceeds the cathode potential: $V_{\text{anode}} > V_{\text{cathode}}$.

For option (A): $V_{\text{anode}} = 0\, \text{V}$, $V_{\text{cathode}} = -4\, \text{V}$, so $0 > -4$ and $0\, \text{V} - (-4\, \text{V}) = +4\, \text{V}$. The diode is forward-biased.

For option (B): $V_{\text{anode}} = -4\, \text{V}$, $V_{\text{cathode}} = -3\, \text{V}$, so $-4 < -3$ and $-4\, \text{V} - (-3\, \text{V}) = -1\, \text{V}$. The diode is reverse-biased.

For option (C): $V_{\text{anode}} = -2\, \text{V}$, $V_{\text{cathode}} = +2\, \text{V}$, so $-2 < 2$ and $-2\, \text{V} - 2\, \text{V} = -4\, \text{V}$. The diode is reverse-biased.

For option (D): $V_{\text{anode}} = +3\, \text{V}$, $V_{\text{cathode}} = +5\, \text{V}$, so $3 < 5$ and $3\, \text{V} - 5\, \text{V} = -2\, \text{V}$. The diode is reverse-biased.

The only forward-biased diode corresponds to option (A).

71625.text: An organic compound 'A' ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$) gives a positive iodoform test but does not reduce Tollens' reagent. Identify the compound 'A':
71625.sol:
The given organic compound 'A' has the molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$.

Since it does not reduce Tollens' reagent, it is not an aldehyde. Therefore, it must be a ketone.

Since it gives a positive iodoform test, it must contain a methyl ketone group ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$).

The only ketone with the molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}$ is propanone (acetone), which is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$.

Note that while propan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHOHCH}_3$) also gives a positive iodoform test and does not reduce Tollens' reagent, its molecular formula is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}$, which does not match the given formula.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$

71978.subject: Chemistry
71978.text: For a solution containing a non-volatile solute in a volatile solvent, which of the following relationships is correctly represented?
71978.sol:
When a non-volatile solute is added to a volatile solvent, the vapor pressure of the solution decreases because a fraction of the surface area is occupied by non-volatile solute particles, reducing the escaping tendency of solvent molecules.

Let $P_1$ be the vapor pressure of the solvent in the solution and $P_1^0$ be the vapor pressure of the pure solvent. According to Raoult's law, the vapor pressure of the solution is directly proportional to the mole fraction of the solvent (X_1$).

$P_1 = P_1^0 X_1$

Since the mole fraction of the solvent in a solution is always less than 1 (X_1 < 1$), it follows that $P_1 < P_1^0$.

Due to the lowering of vapor pressure, the solution must be heated to a higher temperature to make its vapor pressure equal to the external pressure, resulting in an elevation in boiling point (T_b > T_b^0$).

Similarly, the freezing point of the solution is lower than that of the pure solvent, resulting in freezing point depression (T_f < T_f^0$).

Thus, the only correctly represented relationship among the given options is $P_1 < P_1^0$.

Answer: $P_1 < P_1^0$

72209.subject: Physics
72209.text: Three metallic spherical shells (not concentric) of radii R, 2R and 4R are given charges $Q_1$, $Q_2$ and $Q_3$ respectively. It is found that the surface charge densities on the outer surfaces of the shells are equal. Then, the ratio of the charges $Q_1:Q_2:Q_3$, is
72209.sol:
For isolated (not concentric) metallic spherical shells, the charge given to each shell resides entirely on its outer surface.

The surface charge density $\sigma$ of a spherical shell of radius $r$ and charge $Q$ is given by:
$\sigma = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi r^2}$

Given that the surface charge densities on the outer surfaces of the three shells are equal:
$\sigma_1 = \sigma_2 = \sigma_3$

Substituting the values of charges and radii for each shell:
$\dfrac{Q_1}{4\pi R^2} = \dfrac{Q_2}{4\pi (2R)^2} = \dfrac{Q_3}{4\pi (4R)^2}$

$\dfrac{Q_1}{R^2} = \dfrac{Q_2}{4R^2} = \dfrac{Q_3}{16R^2}$

Multiplying by $R^2$, we get the ratio of the charges:
$Q_1 : Q_2 : Q_3 = 1 : 4 : 16$

Answer: $1:4:16$

73793.subject: General Ability
73793.text:
Consider the following statements:
I. A colloid and a suspension are heterogeneous mixtures.
II. Colloids can be separated from the mixture by the process of centrifugation.
III. Particles of colloids and suspensions can be seen by naked eye.
IV. The aqueous solution of copper sulphate does not show Tyndall effect; however, the mixture of milk and water shows Tyndall effect.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
73793.sol:
Statement I is correct. Both colloids and suspensions are heterogeneous mixtures, even though colloids may appear homogeneous to the naked eye.

Statement II is correct. The particles of a colloid are too small to be separated by ordinary filtration, but they can be separated using the process of centrifugation.

Statement III is incorrect. While the particles of a suspension are large enough to be seen by the naked eye, the particles of a colloid are too small to be individually seen by the naked eye.

Statement IV is correct. An aqueous solution of copper sulphate is a true solution and its particles are too small to scatter a beam of light, hence it does not show the Tyndall effect. A mixture of milk and water is a colloid, which contains particles large enough to scatter light, thus showing the Tyndall effect.

75124.text:
Consider the following countries:
I. Haiti
II. Philippines
III. Nicaragua
IV. India
According to the Climate Risk Index 2026, which of the above countries were affected by recurring extreme events during 1995-2024?
75124.sol:
The Global Climate Risk Index analyzes the extent to which countries have been affected by weather-related loss events such as storms, floods, and heatwaves.

Haiti and Nicaragua are highly vulnerable to recurrent hurricanes and extreme weather events in their respective regions.

The Philippines is located in the Pacific typhoon belt, making it highly susceptible to frequent and severe typhoons.

India consistently faces recurring extreme events including severe monsoon floods, cyclones, and heatwaves, placing it among the countries most affected by long-term climate risks.

Therefore, according to climate risk indices assessing long-term vulnerability, all the listed countries namely Haiti, Philippines, Nicaragua, and India have been significantly affected by recurring extreme weather events.

76589.subject: Mathematics
76589.text: What is the greatest value of $r$ satisfying the inequality $\binom{15}{r+1} > 2\times{}^{15}C_r$ ?
76589.sol:
Given inequality is ^{15}C_{r+1} > 2 \times ^{15}C_r$

Using the property ^{n}C_{r+1} = \dfrac{n-r}{r+1} ^{n}C_r$, we get:

$\dfrac{15-r}{r+1} ^{15}C_r > 2 \times ^{15}C_r$

Since ^{15}C_r > 0$, we can divide both sides by ^{15}C_r$:

$\dfrac{15-r}{r+1} > 2$

$15 - r > 2(r + 1)$

$15 - r > 2r + 2$

$3r < 13$

$r < \dfrac{13}{3}$

$r < 4.33$

Since $r$ must be an integer, the greatest possible value of $r$ is $4$.

Answer: $4$

77204.text:
Let $\mathrm{f}: \mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{R}$ be a function such that
$f(x)=x^3+x^2 f^{\prime}(1)+x f f^{\prime \prime}(2)+f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)$
for $\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}$
What is $\mathrmf^{\prime}(1)$ equal to?
77204.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& f(x)=x^3+x^2 f^{\prime}(1)+\mathrm{x} f^{\prime \prime}(2)+f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)...(1) \\
& f^{\prime}(x)=3 x^2+2 x f^{\prime}(1)+f^{\prime \prime}(2)...(2) \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(x)=6 \mathrm{x}+2 f^{\prime}(1)...(3) \\
& f^{\prime \prime \prime}(\mathrm{x})=6...(4) \\
& f^{\prime}(1)=3+2 f^{\prime}(1)+f^{\prime \prime}(2)...(5) \\
& f^{\prime}(2)=12+2 f^{\prime}(1)...(6)
\end{aligned}$
Using (6) in (5), we get
$\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(1)=3+2 f^{\prime}(1)+12+2 f^{\prime \prime}(1)-3 f^{\prime}(1)=15 \\
& f^{\prime}(1)=-5
\end{aligned}$
Using this value in eqn (6) we get
$\begin{aligned}
& f^{\prime}(2)=12+2 \times(-5) \\
& f^{\prime \prime}(2)=2
\end{aligned}$
Using $x=3$ in eqn (4),
$f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)=6$
Putting value of $f^{\prime}(1)+f^{\prime \prime}(2) and f^{\prime \prime \prime}(3)$ in eqn (1) We get
$\begin{aligned}
f(x) & =x^3+x^2(-5)+x(2)+6 \\
& =x^3-5 x^2+2 x+6
\end{aligned}$
Putting $x=1\begin{aligned}
& f(1)=(1)^3-5(1)^2+2(1)+6 \\
& f(1)=4
\end{aligned}$

82583.subject: Physics
82583.text: A long solenoid of diameter $0 . 1m$ has $2 \times {10}^{4}$ turns per meter. At the centre of the solenoid, a coil of $100$ turns and radius $0 . 01m$ is placed with its axis coinciding with the solenoid axis. The current in the solenoid reduces at a constant rate to $0A$ from $4A$ in $0 . 05s$. If the resistance of the coil is $10{\pi}^{2}Ω,$ the total charge flowing through the coil during this time is
82583.sol:
In the given case, the solenoid produces a changing magnetic field. This field is linked with the coil inside and hence, there is an induced emf in the coil.

We have, from the laws of EMI:

$ε = - N\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}$

$\left|\dfrac{ε}{R}\right| = \dfrac{N}{R}\dfrac{dϕ}{dt}$

The ratio given above is the induced current in the circuit which can further be written as the rate of flow of charge per unit time.

$dq = \dfrac{N}{R}dϕ$

$\DeltaQ = \dfrac{N\left(\Deltaϕ\right)}{R}$

$\DeltaQ = \dfrac{\Delta{ϕ}_{total}}{R}$

$= \dfrac{\left(NBA\right)}{R}$

$= \dfrac{N{\text{\mu}_{0} ni\text{\pi}{r}^{2}}{R}$

Putting values

$= \dfrac{100 \times \left(4\pi \times {10}^{- 7}\right) \times \left(2 \times {10}^{4}\right) \times 4 \times \left[{\pi \times ( 0.01 )}^{2}\right]}{10{\text{\pi}}^{2}}$

$\DeltaQ = 32\mu C$

84266.text: Which one of the following does not act as a neurotransmitter?
84266.sol:
Cortisone a steroid, a drug that lowers inflammation is a corticosteroid is a pro-hormone that must be reduced to cortisol in order to bind to and activate the glucocorticoid receptor. Acetylcholine, epinephrine and norepinephrine are neurotransmitters.
Related Theory
Neurotransmitters are often referred to as the body's chemical messengers. They are the molecules used by the nervous system to transmit messages between neurons, or from neurons to muscles. Communication between two neurons happens in the synaptic cleft. Here, electrical signals that have travelled along the axon are briefly converted into chemical ones through the release of neurotransmitters, causing a specific response in the receiving neuron.

85198.subject: Zoology
85198.text: In a cross between a male and female, both heterozygous for sickle cell anaemia gene, what percentage of the progeny will be diseased?
85198.sol:
Since both the parents are heterozygous for sickle-cell anaemia, i.e., shows sickle-cell trait, they are represented by the symbol ${Hb}^{A}{Hb}_{}^{S}$. Each parent thus will produce two types of gametes; one having a composition ${Hb}^{A}$ and the other having a composition for sickle cell anaemia as ${Hb}^{S}$. The progeny cross will be as follows:

Progeny:

${Hb}^{A}$ ${Hb}^{S}$
${Hb}^{A}$ ${Hb}^{A}{Hb}^{A}$
(Normal)		 ${Hb}^{A}{Hb}^{S}$
(Sickle-cell trait)
${Hb}^{S}$ ${Hb}^{A}{Hb}^{S}$
(Sickle-cell trait)		 ${Hb}^{S}{Hb}^{S}$
(Diseased)

Phenotypic ratio: Normal: Sickle-cell trait: Diseased: $1: 2: 1$
Thus, $25 %$ of the progeny will be affected.

85326.text: A male human is heterozygous for autosomal genes $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ and is also hemizygous for hemophilic gene $h$. What proportion of his sperms will be $a b h$ ?

Genotype of male $=\mathrm{AaBbX} \mathrm{X}^{\mathrm{h}} \mathrm{Y}$
Number of gametes $=2^n$
Where $\mathrm{n}=$ no. of heterozygous alleles (genes A, B, sex chromosome)
Thus, Number of gametes $=(2)^3=8$
The gametes produced wil be $=\mathrm{abX}^{\mathrm{h}}$, $a b Y, \mathrm{ABX}^{\mathrm{h}}, \mathrm{aBY}, \mathrm{aBX}{ }^{\mathrm{h}}, \mathrm{AbY}, \mathrm{ABY}$ and $\mathrm{AbX}^{\mathrm{h}}$.
Hence, number of sperm carrying $\mathrm{abh}=1 / 8$.

89043.text: A compound contains three elements X, Y and Z. The oxidation number of X, Y and Z are $+ 3, + 5$ and $- 2$ respectively. The possible formula of the compound is
89043.sol:
The sum of all oxidation values must be equal to zero. Let, number of atoms of X, Y and Z are respectively a, b and c.

Then, $( + 3 ) ext{a} + ( + 5 ) ext{b} + ( - 2 ) ext{c} = 0$

Or

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

Now, putting values of a, b and c for all the given options, which will give sum equal to zero, will be our formula.

(a) For, ${ ext{X}_{2} ext{Y} ext{Z}$

$ ext{a} = 2$

$ ext{b} = 1$

$ ext{c} = 1$

Thus, $3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$3 imes 2 + 5 - 2 e 0$

(b) For, $ ext{X} ext{Y}{ ext{Z}_{3}$

$ ext{a} = 1, ext{b} = 1, ext{c} = 3$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$3 + 5 - 6 e 0$

(c) ${ ext{X}_{3}{( ext{Y}{ ext{Z}_{4} )}_{3}$

$ ext{a} = 3, ext{b} = 3, ext{c} = 12$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$( 3 imes 3 + 5 imes 3 ) - ( 2 imes 12 ) = 0$

$9 + 15 - 24$

$24 - 24 = 0$

(d) ${ ext{X}_{2}{ ext{Y}_{2} ext{Z}$

$ ext{a} = 2, ext{b} = 2, ext{c} = 1$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$( 3 imes 2 ) + ( 5 imes 2 ) - ( 2 imes 1 ) = 0$

$6 + 10 - 2 e 0$

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

90777.text: The line $2x + y = 3$ cuts the ellipse $4{x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 5$ at $P$ and $Q$ . If $\theta$ is the acute angle between normal at $P$ and tangent at $Q$, then $\theta$ is equal to
90777.sol:
Solving $y = 3 - 2x$ and $4{x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 5$ , we get the intersection point $P\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, 2\right)$ and $Q\left(1, 1\right)$
The equation of tangent at these points are $4x\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + 2y = 5$ and $4\left(x\right)\left(1\right) + y\left(1\right) = 5$
$⇒$ Slope of tangents at $P$ and $Q$ are $- 1$ and $- 4$ respectively
$⇒$ Slope of normal at $P$ is $1$
$⇒ tan ⁡ \theta = \left|\dfrac{1 - \left(- 4\right)}{1 + 1\left(- 4\right)}\right| = \dfrac{5}{3} ⇒ cos ⁡ \theta = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{34}}$

91218.text: The value of ${\lim_{x \to \infty} ⁡ \left[\dfrac{e^{2}}{{\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{x}\right)}^{x}}\right]}^{\dfrac{x}{2}}$ is equal to
91218.sol:
Let,& $L = \lim_{x \to \infty}\left[\dfrac{e2}{\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{x}\right)x}\right]\dfrac{x}{2}$

Put $\dfrac{1}{x} = y$

$L = \lim_{y \to {0}^{+}}\left[\dfrac{e2}{\left(1 + 2y\right)\dfrac{1}{y}}\right]\dfrac{1}{2y}$

$L = e^{\lim_{y \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{1}{2y}ln ⁡ \left(\dfrac{e2}{\left(1 + 2y\right)\dfrac{1}{y}}\right)} = e^{M}$ (let)
Now, we have,
$M = \lim_{y \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{1}{2y}ln\left[\dfrac{e2}{\left(1 + 2y\right)\dfrac{1}{y}}\right] = \lim_{y \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{lne^{2} - \dfrac{1}{y}ln\left(1 + 2y\right)}{2y}$
$= \lim_{y \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{2y - ln\left(1 + 2y\right)}{2y^{2}}$
$= \lim_{y \to {0}^{+}}\dfrac{2y - \left(2y - \dfrac{4y^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{8y^{3}}{3} - \dfrac{16y^{4}}{4} + ⋯\right)}{2y^{2}}$
$= \lim_{y \to {0}^{+}} ⁡ \dfrac{2}{2} - \dfrac{4y}{3} + \dfrac{8y^{2}}{4} - . . . . . . = 1$
Hence, $L = e^{1} = e$

$5{λ}^{2} + 24\lambda = 0 ⇒ \lambda = 0, - \dfrac{24}{5}$

96492.subject: Botany
96492.text: Which of the following is corrcet regarding the ecosystem?
options: There is cyclic exchange of materials between living beings and environment.
The flow of energy is unidirectional.
96492.sol:
&

The ecosystem is defined as a system consists of a living community of plants, animals, and microbes together with their physical environment of air, water, soil, etc.

An ecosystem maintains a functional balance amongst its various components. This phenomenon is called homeostasis. The homeostasis or balance of nature is maintained through some control systems like carrying capacity of the ecosystem, the capacity of an ecosystem to recycle the wastes, feedback system, etc.

A functioning ecosystem exhibits biological and chemical activities, rates of plant production, the flow of energy, carbon storage, and nutrient cycling that are characteristic of most forests.

The energy flow in an ecosystem is said to be unidirectional because 90% of the energy gets used up by the organism in a trophic level and is released as heat, and only 10% of the energy is available to be transferred to next trophic level.&

98397.sol: Prosthetic groups are organic compounds and are distinguished from other cofactors in that they are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. For example, in peroxidase and catalase, which catalyze the breakdown of hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen, haem is the prosthetic group and it is a part of the active site of the enzyme. Co-enzymes are also organic compounds but their association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis. Furthermore, co-enzymes serve as co-factors in a number of different enzyme catalyzed reactions. The essential chemical components of many coenzymes are vitamins, e.g., coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and NADP contain the vitamin niacin. Catalytic activity is lost when the co-factor is removed from the enzyme which testifies that they play a crucial role in the catalytic activity of the enzyme.

100889.subject: Physics
100889.text: A particle moves along a straight line such that its position varies with time as $x = t^2 + t$ (where $x$ is in metres and $t$ is in seconds). The instantaneous power delivered to the particle at $t = 2 \text{ s}$ is $50 \text{ W}$. The force acting on the particle at this instant is:
100889.sol:
Given, position of the particle is $x = t^2 + t$

Velocity of the particle is given by:
$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(t^2 + t) = 2t + 1$

At $t = 2 \text{ s}$, the instantaneous velocity is:
$v = 2(2) + 1 = 5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

The instantaneous power is given by $P = Fv$.
Substituting the given values:
$50 = F \times 5$
$F = 10 \text{ N}$

Answer: $10 \text{ N}$

100913.subject: Physics
100913.text: An object with an initial kinetic energy of $20 \text{ J}$ is subjected to a constant force $\vec{F} = (4 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}) \text{ N}$. Under the influence of this force, the object undergoes a displacement $\Delta \vec{r} = (6 \hat{i} + 8 \hat{j}) \text{ m}$. The kinetic energy of the object at the end of this displacement is
100913.sol:
According to the work-energy theorem, the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy: $W = K_f - K_i$.

The work done by the constant force is given by the dot product of the force and displacement vectors:
$W = \vec{F} \cdot \Delta \vec{r} = (4 \hat{i} - 3 \hat{j}) \cdot (6 \hat{i} + 8 \hat{j})$
$W = (4)(6) + (-3)(8) = 24 - 24 = 0 \text{ J}$

Since the force and displacement vectors are orthogonal, the work done is zero.

Using the work-energy theorem:
$0 = K_f - 20$

101377.subject: Physics
101377.text: Two satellites A and B are orbiting a planet in circular orbits. The time period of revolution of satellite B is 8 times that of satellite A. If the orbital radius of satellite A is $R$, what is the orbital radius of satellite B?
101377.sol:
According to Kepler's Third Law, the square of the time period is proportional to the cube of the orbital radius, i.e., $T^2 \propto r^3$.

This can be rearranged to find the radius dependence on the time period: $r \propto T^{2/3}$.

Taking the ratio for satellites B and A:
$\dfrac{r_B}{r_A} = \left(\dfrac{T_B}{T_A}\right)^{2/3}$

Given $T_B = 8 T_A$ and $r_A = R$:
$\dfrac{r_B}{R} = (8)^{2/3} = (2^3)^{2/3} = 2^2 = 4$

Therefore, $r_B = 4R$.

Answer: $4R$

103325.subject: Physics
103325.text: Two batteries and two resistors are connected in series to form a single-loop circuit. The first battery has an unknown EMF $E$ and the second battery has an EMF of $4\text{ V}$. The batteries are connected in opposition. The two resistors have resistances of $2\ \Omega$ and $3\ \Omega$. If a steady current of $2\text{ A}$ flows through the circuit such that it leaves the positive terminal of the first battery, what is the value of the unknown EMF $E$? (Assume the batteries have negligible internal resistance).
103325.sol:
Since the batteries are connected in opposition and the current leaves the positive terminal of the first battery, the first battery dominates. The net EMF in the circuit is $E_{\text{net}} = E - 4$.

The total resistance of the circuit is the sum of the series resistors:
$R_{\text{net}} = 2\ \Omega + 3\ \Omega = 5\ \Omega$.

According to Ohm's law for the complete circuit, the current is:
$I = \dfrac{E_{\text{net}}}{R_{\text{net}}}$

Substituting the given values:
$2 = \dfrac{E - 4}{5}$

$10 = E - 4$

$E = 14\text{ V}$.

Answer: $14\text{ V}$

103912.subject: Physics
103912.text: A metallic rod of length $3.0 \mathrm{~m}$ is hinged at one end and rotated at a constant angular frequency of $100 \mathrm{~rad/s}$ in a uniform magnetic field that is perpendicular to the plane of rotation. If the induced electromotive force developed across the ends of the rod is $90 \mathrm{~V}$, what is the magnitude of the uniform magnetic field?
103912.sol:
The motional emf $\varepsilon$ induced across the ends of a rod of length $L$ rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a perpendicular magnetic field $B$ is given by:
$\varepsilon = \dfrac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$

Rearranging the formula to solve for the magnetic field $B$, we get:
$B = \dfrac{2\varepsilon}{\omega L^2}$

Given values are:
$\varepsilon = 90 \mathrm{~V}$
$\omega = 100 \mathrm{~rad/s}$
$L = 3.0 \mathrm{~m}$

Substituting these values into the rearranged equation:
$B = \dfrac{2 \times 90}{100 \times (3.0)^2}$
$B = \dfrac{180}{100 \times 9}$
$B = \dfrac{180}{900} = 0.2 \mathrm{~T}$

If the factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ is forgotten, the result would incorrectly be $0.1 \mathrm{~T}$. If the length is not squared, the result would incorrectly be $0.6 \mathrm{~T}$.

Answer: $0.2 \mathrm{~T}$

109399.text:
Match List-I with List-II for the $\text{pH}$ of various equal-volume mixtures.
[Given: $\text{pK}_\text{a}$ of weak acid $\text{HA} = 4.0$, $\text{pK}_\text{b}$ of weak base $\text{BOH} = 5.0$ at $298 \text{ K}$]

List-I (Mixture)List-II (pH)
(A) $0.1 \text{ M HA} + 0.1 \text{ M NaA}$(I) $3.0$
(B) $0.1 \text{ M HA} + 1.0 \text{ M NaA}$(II) $4.0$
(C) $1.0 \text{ M HA} + 0.1 \text{ M NaA}$(III) $5.0$
(D) $0.1 \text{ M BOH} + 0.1 \text{ M BCl}$(IV) $9.0$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
109399.sol:
For acidic buffers, $\text{pH} = \text{pK}_\text{a} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Acid}]} \right)$

(A) $[\text{Salt}] = [\text{Acid}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$.
$\text{pH} = 4.0 + \log(1) = 4.0$

(B) $[\text{Salt}] = 1.0 \text{ M}$, $[\text{Acid}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$.
$\text{pH} = 4.0 + \log\left(\dfrac{1.0}{0.1}\right) = 4.0 + \log(10) = 5.0$

(C) $[\text{Salt}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$, $[\text{Acid}] = 1.0 \text{ M}$.
$\text{pH} = 4.0 + \log\left(\dfrac{0.1}{1.0}\right) = 4.0 - 1 = 3.0$

For basic buffers, $\text{pOH} = \text{pK}_\text{b} + \log \left( \dfrac{[\text{Salt}]}{[\text{Base}]} \right)$

(D) $[\text{Salt}] = [\text{Base}] = 0.1 \text{ M}$.
$\text{pOH} = 5.0 + \log(1) = 5.0$
$\text{pH} = 14 - \text{pOH} = 14 - 5.0 = 9.0$

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)

111885.subject: Chemistry
111885.text:
What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound given below?

$HC \equiv C - CH(CH_2CH_3) - CH_2 - CH(CH_3) - CH_2 - CH_3$
111885.sol:
The principal functional group is the alkyne (triple bond), so the longest carbon chain containing the triple bond is selected as the parent chain. Here, the longest chain has 7 carbon atoms, making it a heptane derivative.

Numbering must be done from the end closer to the triple bond to give it the lowest possible locant. Thus, numbering starts from left to right, placing the triple bond at C1.

The substituents are an ethyl group at C3 and a methyl group at C5.

According to IUPAC rules, substituents are cited in alphabetical order. Ethyl comes before methyl.

Combining these parts, the correct IUPAC name is 3-Ethyl-5-methylhept-1-yne.

Answer: 3-Ethyl-5-methylhept-1-yne

114905.subject: Chemistry
114905.text:
For a zero-order reaction $2\text{A} \rightarrow 3\text{B}$ with rate constant $k$, consider the following statements:

(I) The rate of disappearance of A is $2k$.
(II) The half-life of the reaction is $\dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{2k}$.
(III) The rate of appearance of B is $3k$.
(IV) The reaction goes to $100\%$ completion in time $t = \dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{k}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
114905.sol:
For the zero-order reaction $2\text{A} \rightarrow 3\text{B}$, the rate of reaction is given by:

$\text{Rate} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\text{A}]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{d[\text{B}]}{dt} = k$

Statement (I): The rate of disappearance of A is $-\dfrac{d[\text{A}]}{dt} = 2k$. This statement is correct.

Statement (III): The rate of appearance of B is $\dfrac{d[\text{B}]}{dt} = 3k$. This statement is correct.

The integrated rate law for this reaction is:
$[\text{A}]_0 - [\text{A}]_t = 2kt$

Statement (II): At half-life ($t_{1/2}$), $[\text{A}]_t = \dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{2}$.
$\dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{2} = 2kt_{1/2} \Rightarrow t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{4k}$.
This statement is incorrect.

Statement (IV): For $100\%$ completion, $[\text{A}]_t = 0$.
$[\text{A}]_0 = 2kt \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{[\text{A}]_0}{2k}$.
This statement is incorrect.

Exactly two statements (I and III) are correct.

Answer: 2

117748.subject: Chemistry
117748.text:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Complex)List-II (Spin-only magnetic moment)
(A) $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$(I) $0$ BM
(B) $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$(II) $1.73$ BM
(C) $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$(III) $4.90$ BM
(D) $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$(IV) $5.92$ BM

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
117748.sol:
For $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$:
Fe is in $+2$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Fe$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^6$.
H$_2$O is a weak field ligand, so pairing does not occur. The configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 4$.
$\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ BM.

For $[\text{Mn(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$:
Mn is in $+2$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Mn$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^5$.
H$_2$O is a weak field ligand. The configuration is $t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 5$.
$\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.

For $[\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}$:
Ni is in $+2$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Ni$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.
CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing. The complex is square planar ($dsp^2$) with all electrons paired.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 0$.
$\mu = 0$ BM.

For $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$:
Cu is in $+2$ oxidation state. The electronic configuration of Cu$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^9$.
It has one unpaired electron regardless of the ligand field.
Number of unpaired electrons, $n = 1$.
$\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ BM.

Thus, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

119267.subject: Chemistry
119267.text: An organic compound X ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) gives a red-orange precipitate with $2,4$-DNP reagent and a yellow precipitate upon heating with iodine and aqueous $\text{NaOH}$. Drastic oxidation of X with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$ followed by acidification yields a dicarboxylic acid Y. Upon heating, compound Y readily loses a molecule of water to produce an anhydride Z. The compound X is:
119267.sol:
Compound X ($\text{C}_9\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$) forms a red-orange precipitate with $2,4$-DNP, indicating the presence of a carbonyl group.

It gives a yellow precipitate with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$ (iodoform test), confirming the presence of a methyl ketone ($-\text{COCH}_3$) group.

Drastic oxidation of X yields a dicarboxylic acid Y, meaning there are two oxidizable side chains on the benzene ring. Since X has $9$ carbon atoms and contains a $-\text{COCH}_3$ group ($2$ carbons), the remaining $7$ carbons must form a methylphenyl group. Thus, X is a methylacetophenone isomer.

Heating Y produces an anhydride Z, which is characteristic of ortho-dicarboxylic acids (like phthalic acid). This implies the two side chains in X must be ortho to each other.

Therefore, X is $1$-(2-methylphenyl)ethanone (o-methylacetophenone).

Option 2 gives terephthalic acid (which does not form an anhydride on simple heating). Option 3 gives isophthalic acid (no anhydride). Option 4 (propiophenone) fails the iodoform test and yields a monocarboxylic acid (benzoic acid) on oxidation.

Answer: $1$-(2-Methylphenyl)ethanone

119877.subject: Chemistry
119877.text:
Given below are two statements:
Assertion (A): N-methylethanamide on treatment with bromine and ethanolic sodium hydroxide gives N-methylmethanamine.
Reason (R): Hoffmann bromamide degradation is given only by primary amides.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
119877.sol:
N-methylethanamide (CH$_3$CONHCH$_3$) is a secondary amide. The Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction is a characteristic reaction of primary amides (R-CONH$_2$) only. Secondary and tertiary amides do not undergo this reaction.

Therefore, N-methylethanamide will not undergo degradation with bromine and ethanolic sodium hydroxide to yield N-methylmethanamine. Thus, Assertion (A) is false.

Reason (R) correctly states that the reaction is specific to primary amides, which is a true statement.

Hence, Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

121362.sol: Commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known. Once perfect (sexual) stages of members of dueteromycetes were discovered they were often moved to ascomycetesand basidiomycetes. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> The deuteromycetes reproduce only by asexual spores known as conidia. </mark>  The mycelium is septate and branched. 121786.subject: Botany
121786.text: Into what two groups are bryophytes divided?
121786.sol: Bryophytes in general are of little economic importance but some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals, birds and other animals. Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water. Mosses along with lichens are the first organisms to colonize rocks and hence, are of great ecological importance. They decompose rocks making the substrate suitable for the growth of higher plants. Since moses form dense mats on the soil, they reduce the impact of falling rain and prevent soil erosion. <mark>The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses.</mark>Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes. In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is a precursor to the seed habit considered an important step in evolution. The pteridophytes are further classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

122718.subject: Botany
122718.text: What is the name given to the swollen leaf base in leguminous plants?
122718.sol: A typical leaf consists of three main parts: leaf base, petiole and lamina (Figure 5.4 a). The leaf is attached to the stem by the leaf base and may bear two lateral small leaf like structures called stipules. In monocotyledons, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly. In some leguminous plants the leafbase may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus. The petiole help hold the blade to light. Long thin flexible petioles allow leaf blades to flutter in wind, thereby cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to leaf surface. The lamina or the leaf blade is the green expanded part of the leaf with veins and veinlets. There is, usually, a middle prominent vein, which is known as the midrib. Veins provide rigidity to the leaf blade and act as channels of transport for water, minerals and food materials. The shape, margin, apex, surface and extent of incision of lamina varies in different leaves.

122933.subject: Botany
122933.text:
Match the type of placentation in Column I with its corresponding structural characteristic and plant example in Column II.
Column IColumn II
(a) Axile(i) False septum formation in a unilocular ovary; Mustard
(b) Parietal(ii) Single ovule attached at the ovary base; Sunflower
(c) Free central(iii) Multilocular ovary with central attachment; Lemon
(d) Basal(iv) Septa are completely absent; Dianthus
Select the correct answer from the options given below.
122933.sol:
Refer: NCERT | Class 11 | Page: 65 | Paragraph: 2

Axile placentation occurs in a multilocular ovary where ovules are attached to the central axis. Example: Lemon. Thus, (a) matches (iii).

Parietal placentation occurs when ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary. A false septum may form, making the unilocular ovary bilocular. Example: Mustard. Thus, (b) matches (i).

Free central placentation features ovules borne on a central axis with septa completely absent. Example: Dianthus. Thus, (c) matches (iv).

Basal placentation involves a single ovule attached at the base of the ovary. Example: Sunflower. Thus, (d) matches (ii).

The correct matching is (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

Answer: (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii)

122984.sol:
Statement (I) is correct: In China rose, the stamens are united into a single bundle, which is termed monadelphous.

Statement (II) is correct: In pea, the stamens are united into two bundles, termed diadelphous.

Statement (III) is correct: In Citrus, the stamens are united into more than two bundles, termed polyadelphous.

Statement (IV) is incorrect: In lily, the stamens are attached to the perianth, a condition known as epiphyllous, not epipetalous. Epipetalous condition (attachment to petals) is seen in brinjal.

Therefore, only statements (I), (II) and (III) are correct.

123534.subject: Botany
123534.text: What is the function of the cell cycle?
options: To ensure the integrity of the genome in progeny cells
123534.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed cell cycle. Although cell growth (in terms of cytoplasmic increase) is a continuous process, DNA synthesis occurs only during one specific stage in the cell cycle.

124925.subject: Botany
124925.text: What is the primary function of the cells in the interior of thick, woody stems?
124925.sol: Each living cell in a plant is located quite close to the surface of the plant. ‘This is true for leaves’, you may ask, ‘but what about thick, woody stems and roots?’ In stems, the ‘living’ cells are organized in thin layers inside and beneath the bark. They also have openings called lenticels. The cells in the interior are dead and provide only mechanical support. Thus, most cells of a plant have at least a part of their surface in contact with air. This is also facilitated by the loose packing of parenchyma cells in leaves, stems and roots, which provide an interconnected network of air spaces.
