125363.subject: Botany
125363.text: What are the main components of the membrane system in chloroplasts that are involved in the light reactions?
125363.sol: While the membrane or lamellae of the grana have both PS I and PS II the stroma lamellae membranes lack PS II as well as NADP reductase enzyme. The excited electron does not pass on to NADP+ but is cycled back to the PS I complex through the electron transport chain (Figure 11.6). The cyclic flow hence, results only in the synthesis of ATP, but not of NADPH + H+ . Cyclic photophosphorylation also occurs when only light of wavelengths beyond 680 nm are available for excitation.

125471.text: What are the internal factors dependent on?

125471.sol: An understanding of the factors that affect photosynthesis is necessary. The rate of photosynthesis is very important in determining the yield of plants including crop plants. Photosynthesis is under the influence of several factors, both internal (plant) and external. The plant factors include the number, size, age and orientation of leaves, mesophyll cells and chloroplasts, internal CO2 concentration and the amount of chlorophyll. The plant or internal factors are dependent on the genetic predisposition and the growth of the plant.

125846.subject: Botany
125846.text: When multiple pistils are fused together, what is the condition called?
125846.sol: The gynoecium represents the female reproductive part of the flower. The gynoecium may consist of a single pistil (monocarpellary) or may have more than one pistil (multicarpellary). When there are more than one, the pistils may be fused together (syncarpous) or may be free (apocarpous) Each pistil has three parts the stigma, style and ovary. The stigma serves as a landing platform for pollen grains. The style is the elongated slender part beneath the stigma. The basal bulged part of the pistil is the ovary. Inside the ovary is the ovarian cavity (locule). The placenta is located inside the ovarian cavity. Recall the definition and types of placentation that you studied in Arising from the placenta are the megasporangia, commonly called ovules. The number of ovules in an ovary may be one (wheat, paddy, mango) to many (papaya, water melon, orchids). The Megasporangium (Ovule).

125887.subject: Botany
125887.text: What feature of the corn cob demonstrates wind pollination?
options: The large number of ovules in each ovary
The sticky nature of the pollen grains
The tassels that wave in the wind
The enclosed nature of the flowers
125887.sol: Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollinations. Wind pollination also requires that the pollen grains are light and non-sticky so that they can be transported in wind currents. They often possess well-exposed stamens (so that the pollens are easily dispersed into wind currents, and large often-feathery stigma to easily trap air-borne pollen grains. Wind- pollinated flowers often have a single ovule in each ovary and numerous flowers packed into an inflorescence; a familiar example is the corn cob – the tassels you see are nothing but the stigma and style which wave in the wind to trap pollen grains. Wind-pollination is quite common in grasses.

128276.subject: Zoology
128276.text: What is the role of GnRH in the regulation of pituitary hormone synthesis and secretion?
options: It stimulates the release of gonadotrophins
It inhibits the release of gonadotrophins
It stimulates the release of growth hormone
It inhibits the release of growth hormone
128276.sol: The hypothalamic hormone called Gonadotrophin releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulates the pituitary synthesis and release of gonadotrophins. On the other hand, somatostatin from the hypothalamus inhibits the release of growth hormone from the pituitary. These hormones originating in the hypothalamic neurons, pass through axons and are released from their nerve endings. These hormones reach the pituitary gland through a portal circulatory system and regulate the functions of the anterior pituitary. The posterior pituitary is under the direct neural regulation of the hypothalamus.

128397.subject: Zoology
128397.text: What is the effect of hormone-receptor complex formation on target tissues?
options: It leads to the formation of second messengers
It regulates gene expression or chromosome function
It leads to certain biochemical changes in the target tissue
It leads to physiological and developmental effects
128397.sol: Hormones produce their effects on target tissues by binding to specific proteins called hormone receptors located in the target tissues only. Hormone receptors present on the cell membrane of the target cells are called membrane-bound receptors and the receptors present inside the target cell are called intracellular receptors, mostly nuclear receptors (present in the nucleus). Binding of a hormone to its receptor leads to the formation of a hormone-receptor complex (Figure 19.5 a, b). Each receptor is specific to one hormone only and hence receptors are specific. Hormone-Receptor complex formation leads to certain biochemical changes in the target tissue. Target tissue metabolism and hence physiological functions are regulated by hormones. Hormones which interact with membrane-bound receptors normally do not enter the target cell, but generate second messengers (e.g., cyclic AMP, IP3, Ca++ etc) which in turn regulate cellular metabolism (Figure 19.5a). Hormones which interact with intracellular receptors (e.g., steroid hormones, iodothyronines, etc.) mostly regulate gene expression or chromosome function by the interaction of hormone-receptor complex with the genome. Cumulative biochemical actions result in physiological and developmental effects (Figure 19.5b).

128827.subject: Zoology
128827.sol: Blood exhibits coagulation or clotting in response to an injury or trauma. This is a mechanism to prevent excessive loss of blood from the body. You would have observed a dark reddish brown scum formed at the site of a cut or an injury over a period of time. It is a clot or coagulam formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped. Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin. Thrombins, in turn are formed from another inactive substance present in the plasma called prothrombin. An enzyme complex, thrombokinase, is required for the above reaction. This complex is formed by a series of linked enzymic reactions (cascadeprocess) involving a number of factors present in the plasma in an inactive state. An injury or a trauma stimulates the platelets in the blood to release certain factors which activate the mechanism of coagulation. Certain factors released by the tissues at the site of injury also can initiate coagulation. Calcium ions play a very important role in clotting

129039.subject: Zoology
129039.text:
Read the following statements regarding erythroblastosis foetalis:
(A) It occurs due to Rh incompatibility between an Rh-negative mother and an Rh-positive foetus.
(B) The maternal immune system is typically exposed to the foetal Rh antigen during the first trimester of the first pregnancy.
(C) The condition leads to severe anaemia and jaundice in the affected baby.
(D) It can be prevented by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child.

How many of the above statements are correct?
129039.sol:
Statement (A) is correct as erythroblastosis foetalis is a special case of Rh incompatibility between an Rh-negative mother and an Rh-positive foetus.

Statement (B) is incorrect because the foetal and maternal blood are normally kept well separated by the placenta during pregnancy. Exposure to the Rh antigen typically occurs at the time of birth of the first child, not during the first trimester.

Statement (C) is correct as the destruction of foetal red blood cells by maternal antibodies causes severe anaemia and jaundice in the newborn.

Statement (D) is correct as the standard preventive measure is administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the first child to prevent maternal sensitization.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

129805.sol: whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Exchange part is the site of actual diffusion of O2 and CO2 between blood and atmospheric air. The lungs are situated in the thoracic chamber which is anatomically an air-tight chamber. The thoracic chamber is formed dorsally by the vertebral column, ventrally by the sternum, laterally by the ribs and on the lower side by the dome-shaped diaphragm. 130236.subject: Zoology
130236.text: What makes the matrix of bones hard in the human body?
130236.sol: The matrix of bones in the human body is hard due to the presence of calcium salts. This makes bones strong enough to support the weight of the body and protect delicate organs. Cartilages in the Skeletal system are specialised connective tissues that have a slightly pliable matrix due to chondroitin salts. This makes them ideal for joints where bones need to move smoothly against each other.The Skeletal system is grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton which includes the bones that make up the central axis of the body such as the skull, spinal column, rib cage and the appendicular skeleton which includes bones of the upper and lower limbs and the bones that attach the limbs to the axial skeleton. Bones play a crucial role in supporting and providing structure to the human body. They also protect delicate organs, store minerals, and produce blood cells.

131803.subject: Zoology
131803.text: In a eukaryotic transcription unit, the promoter is located towards the $5'$ end of the coding strand. Which strand's sequence does the newly formed hnRNA resemble, and to which end of this hnRNA are adenylate residues added during post-transcriptional processing?
131803.sol:
During transcription, the DNA strand with $3' \rightarrow 5'$ polarity acts as the template, while the strand with $5' \rightarrow 3'$ polarity is the coding strand. The newly synthesized hnRNA is complementary to the template strand, which means its sequence is identical to the coding strand (with uracil replacing thymine).

During post-transcriptional processing in eukaryotes, tailing involves the addition of $200-300$ adenylate residues to the $3'$ end of the hnRNA in a template-independent manner. Capping (addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate) occurs at the $5'$ end.

Therefore, the hnRNA resembles the coding strand, and adenylate residues are added to its $3'$ end.

Answer: Coding strand; $3'$ end

132533.subject: Zoology
132533.text:
Assertion : In humans, the gamete contributed by the male determines whether the child produced will be male or female.
Reason: Sex in humans is a polygenic trait depending upon a cumulative effect of some genes on $\mathrm{X}$-chromosome and some on Y-chromosome.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
132533.sol: Sex chromosomes in the human female are XX; whereas those of the male are XY. During the very early stages of gestation period, the development of the embryo is predisposed in certain directions by the possession of the sex chromosomes one contributed by the mother and the other by the father. The mother can contribute only X chromosome which predisposes towards the development of female structural, functional and temperamental characteristics, but the father can contribute either an X or a Y chromosome predisposing in the first instance to female or in the second to male structural, functional and temperamental characteristics. In short, the sex of the child to be born is governed by the chromosomal contribution of the father. A child conceived will develop into a female on receiving an $\mathrm{X}$ chromosome from the mother and an X chromosome from the father (XX), or into a male on receiving an $\mathrm{X}$ chromosome from the mother but a $\mathrm{Y}$ chromosome from the father (XY). Therefore, sex in humans is not polygenic.

132894.subject: Zoology
132894.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding evidences for evolution.

List-IList-II
(A) Ernst Haeckel(I) Noted that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals
(B) Karl Ernst von Baer(II) Proposed embryological support based on features common to all vertebrate embryos
(C) Divergent evolution(III) Results in analogous structures like wings of butterfly and birds
(D) Convergent evolution(IV) Results in homologous structures like forelimbs of whales and bats

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
132894.sol:
Ernst Haeckel proposed embryological support for evolution based on the observation of certain features during the embryonic stage common to all vertebrates that are absent in adults.

Karl Ernst von Baer disapproved this proposal after careful study, noting that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.

Divergent evolution results in homologous structures, which share a common ancestry but perform different functions (e.g., forelimbs of whales and bats).

Convergent evolution results in analogous structures, which perform similar functions but have different anatomical origins (e.g., wings of butterfly and birds).

Therefore, the correct matching is (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III).

Answer: (A) - (II), (B) - (I), (C) - (IV), (D) - (III)

133071.sol: To be a mammal the presence of hair and milk or mammary gland is must, but presence of 7 cervical vertebrae and 12 pairs of cranial nerves are also additional mammalian characteristics. The monotremes make up by far the smallest subclass of mammals, with just three species, found in Australia, Tasmania, and New Guinea. One of these is the duck-billed platypus, and the remaining two are the echidnas, or spiny anteaters.The duck-billed platypus and the spiny anteater are mammals that lay eggs rather than give live birth to young ones. The platypus has a bill like a duck, fur like a mammal and webbed feet. It lays eggs that look like reptile eggs. Its young feed from the mother's mammary glands. The spiny anteater's covering looks like that of the porcupine. It has a long tongue to catch insects and a bill. It lays several eggs which it keeps in a pouch on its side.

133571.subject: Zoology
133571.text: A patient undergoes a successful kidney transplant but is prescribed immunosuppressants for the rest of their life to prevent graft rejection. Which specific type of immune response is primarily responsible for this rejection, and to which broader category of immunity does it belong?
133571.sol:
Graft rejection in organ transplantation is primarily mediated by T-lymphocytes, which are responsible for the cell-mediated immune response (CMI).

Cell-mediated immunity is a highly specific immune response that develops during an individual's lifetime and is characterised by immunological memory. Therefore, it is a sub-type of acquired immunity, not innate immunity.

Humoral immunity, mediated by B-lymphocytes (antibodies), is not the primary cause of graft rejection.

Answer: Cell-mediated immunity; Acquired immunity

133630.subject: Zoology
133630.text: When children play bare footed in pools of dirty water and flood water, they may suffer from disease like
options: guinea worm infection, elephantiasis and amoebic dysentery.
133630.sol:
Leptospirosis (also known as Weil's disease, canicola fever, canefield fever, nanukayami fever or 7-day fever) is a bacterial zoonotic disease caused by spirochaetes of the genus Leptospira that affects humans and a wide range of animals, including mammals, birds, amphibians, and reptiles. It was first described by Adolf Weil in 1886 when he reported an "acute infectious disease with enlargement of spleen, jaundice and nephritis.Humans become infected through contact with water, food, or soil containing urine from these infected animals. This may happen by swallowing contaminated food or water or through skin contact. Leptospirosis is common among watersport enthusiasts in certain areas as prolonged immersion in water is known to promote the entry of the bacteria.
Schistosomiasis or bilharzia is al so called snail fever or swimmer's itch. Schistosomiasis is a lifethreatening parasitic disease caused by a worm that lives in a host snail. Humans can become infected when they come in contact with water in ponds and rivers where the snail lives. The pathology is mostly caused by the large number of eggs becoming stuck in various body parts, in particular the liver (causing liver enlargement and malfunction) and the kidneys (causing kidney damage, detectable by blood in the urine).

302618.text: The change in surface energy when a big spherical drop fo radius $R$ is split into $n$ spherical droplets of radius $r$ is $(T=$ surface tension)

(i)] $=4 \$piR^2\left($n^{1 / 3}-1\right)$ The work done for change in area, $W=T $\times \Delta$A=T \times4 \piR^2  \left($n^{1 / 3}-1\right)$ This work is store in the form of energy.

303124.text: A rifle bullet loses \left(\dfrac{1}{25}\right)th$ of its velocity in passing through a plank. The least number of such planks required just to stop the bullet is$
303124.sol:
If& $u$is the initial velocity of bullet then after~passing through one plank the velocity became~$v = u - \dfrac{u}{25} = \dfrac{24u}{25}$

Using kinematic equation for uniform acceleration motion,~$v^{2} - u^{2} = 2as$

\left(\dfrac{24u}{25}\right)2 - u^{2} = 2as ⇒ 2as = \dfrac{u^{2}\left(- 625 + 576\right)}{625} ⇒ 2as = - u^{2}\dfrac{49}{625}$

If~$n$number of planks are required to bring the bullet at rest then,~$v = 0$

$⇒ 0 - u^{2} = 2a\left(ns\right) ⇒ - u^{2} = n\left(\dfrac{- 49u^{2}}{625}\right) ⇒ n = \dfrac{625}{49} = 12 . 75\text{or}13$

Thus,~$13$planks will be required in order to bring the bullet at rest.

$

303552.subject: Physics
303552.text: An ornament weighs $36 \text{ g}$ in air and $34 \text{ g}$ in water. Assuming the ornament is prepared by mixing some copper with gold, determine the amount of copper present in it. The specific gravity of gold is $19.3$ and that of copper is $8.9$.
303552.sol:
Loss of weight of the ornament in water $= 36 - 34 = 2 \text{ g}$

Since the density of water is $1 \text{ g/cm}^3$, the volume of the displaced water is $2 \text{ cm}^3$. Therefore, the total volume of the ornament is $V = 2 \text{ cm}^3$.

Let the mass of copper in the ornament be $m$. Then the mass of gold is $36 - m$.

The volume of copper is $V_c = \dfrac{m}{8.9}$ and the volume of gold is $V_g = \dfrac{36 - m}{19.3}$.

The total volume of the ornament is the sum of the volumes of copper and gold:

$\dfrac{m}{8.9} + \dfrac{36 - m}{19.3} = 2$

$\dfrac{m}{8.9} - \dfrac{m}{19.3} = 2 - \dfrac{36}{19.3}$

$m \left( \dfrac{19.3 - 8.9}{8.9 \times 19.3} \right) = \dfrac{38.6 - 36}{19.3}$

$m \left( \dfrac{10.4}{8.9 \times 19.3} \right) = \dfrac{2.6}{19.3}$

$m = \dfrac{2.6 \times 8.9}{10.4}$

$m = \dfrac{8.9}{4} = 2.225 \text{ g}$

The amount of copper present is approximately $2.2 \text{ g}$.

303668.subject: Physics
303668.text: A $5 \text{ mm}$ high pin is situated at a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from a convex lens of focal length $10 \text{ cm}$. Positioned $40 \text{ cm}$ from the first lens and $55 \text{ cm}$ from the pin is a second lens having a focal length of $5 \text{ cm}$. Identify the nature of the final image.
303668.sol:
For the first lens:

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{u_1} = \dfrac{1}{f_1}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_1} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{1}{30} \Rightarrow v_1 = 30 \text{ cm}$

Magnification of the first lens, $m_1 = \dfrac{v_1}{u_1} = \dfrac{30}{-15} = -2$

The image formed by the first lens acts as the object for the second lens. The distance between the lenses is $40 \text{ cm}$.

Object distance for the second lens, $u_2 = -(40 - 30) = -10 \text{ cm}$

For the second lens:

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{u_2} = \dfrac{1}{f_2}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} - \dfrac{1}{-10} = \dfrac{1}{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{v_2} = \dfrac{1}{5} - \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{10} \Rightarrow v_2 = 10 \text{ cm}$

Since $v_2$ is positive, the final image is real.

Magnification of the second lens, $m_2 = \dfrac{v_2}{u_2} = \dfrac{10}{-10} = -1$

Total magnification, $m = m_1 \times m_2 = (-2) \times (-1) = 2$

Since the total magnification is positive, the final image is erect with respect to the original object.

Thus, the final image is erect and real.

303673.subject: Physics
303673.text: Two convex lenses, each having a focal length of $10 \text{ cm}$, are positioned at a separation of $15 \text{ cm}$ with their principal axes coinciding. Compute the focal length of the equivalent lens. (Note that the sign of the focal length is positive even though the lens system actually diverges a parallel beam incident on it.)
303673.sol:
Given $f_1 = 10 \text{ cm}$, $f_2 = 10 \text{ cm}$, and the distance between the lenses $d = 15 \text{ cm}$.

The equivalent focal length $F$ of two thin lenses separated by a distance $d$ is given by the formula:

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{f_1} + \dfrac{1}{f_2} - \dfrac{d}{f_1 f_2}$

Substituting the given values:

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{15}{10 \times 10}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{2}{10} - \dfrac{15}{100}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{20}{100} - \dfrac{15}{100}$

$\dfrac{1}{F} = \dfrac{5}{100} = \dfrac{1}{20}$

$F = 20 \text{ cm}$

303966.subject: Physics
303966.text: A small block of mass $m$ is placed on a bigger block of mass $M$ that is attached to a vertical spring of spring constant $k$. The system oscillates vertically. Determine the maximum amplitude with which the two blocks can oscillate together without losing contact.
303966.sol:
Let the amplitude of oscillation be $A$.

The angular frequency of the spring-mass system is given by $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{M+m}}$.

The maximum downward acceleration of the system occurs at the highest point of oscillation and its magnitude is $a_{\max} = \omega^2 A = \dfrac{k}{M+m}A$.

Consider the forces acting on the small block of mass $m$ at the highest point: the downward gravitational force $mg$ and the upward normal reaction $N$ from the bigger block.

The equation of motion for the small block is:
$mg - N = m a_{\max}$

For the block of mass $m$ to not lose contact with the block of mass $M$, the normal reaction must be non-negative ($N \ge 0$).

$mg - m a_{\max} \ge 0$
$\Rightarrow a_{\max} \le g$

Substituting the value of $a_{\max}$:
$\dfrac{k}{M+m}A \le g$
$\Rightarrow A \le \dfrac{(M+m)g}{k}$

Thus, the maximum amplitude with which the two blocks can oscillate together is $\dfrac{(M+m)g}{k}$.

304098.subject: Physics
304098.text: Determine the temperature at which the speed of sound is twice its value at $0^{}^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C}$.
304098.sol:
The speed of sound in a gas is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma R T}{M}}$, which implies $v \propto \sqrt{T}$, where $T$ is the absolute temperature.

Let $v_1$ be the speed at $T_1 = 0^{}^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} = 273 \text{ K}$ and $v_2$ be the speed at temperature $T_2$.

Given $v_2 = 2v_1$, we have:

$\dfrac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}} = 2$

$\dfrac{T_2}{T_1} = 4$

$T_2 = 4T_1$

Substituting $T_1 = 273 \text{ K}$:

$T_2 = 4 \times 273 \text{ K} = 1092 \text{ K}$

Converting to Celsius:

$T_2 = 1092 - 273 = 819^{}^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C}$

304418.subject: Physics
304418.text:
Examine the two statements given below:
(A) Line spectra provide information regarding atoms.
(B) Band spectra provide information regarding molecules.
options: Statement (A) is correct, but (B) is incorrect.
Statement (B) is correct, but (A) is incorrect.
304418.sol:
Line spectra are characteristic of atoms. When an atom is excited, its electrons transition between discrete electronic energy levels, producing a spectrum consisting of distinct, separated lines. Thus, line spectra provide information regarding atomic structure.

Band spectra are characteristic of molecules. Molecules possess vibrational and rotational energy levels in addition to electronic energy levels. Transitions between these closely spaced levels produce groups of closely spaced lines that appear as continuous bands. Thus, band spectra provide information regarding molecular structure.

Therefore, both statements (A) and (B) are correct.

304661.sol:

Since a vacuum contains no particles to transmit the wave, sound cannot travel through it.

304813.subject: Physics
304813.chapter: Wave Motion and Waves on a String
options: The energy of any small part of a string remains constant in a travelling wave
The energy of any small part of a string remains constant in a standing wave
The energies of all the small parts of equal length are equal in a travelling wave
The energies of all the small parts of equal length are equal in a standing wave
304813.sol:
In a travelling wave, energy is continuously transmitted along the string.

The energy of a small part of the string in a travelling wave fluctuates with time, as its kinetic and potential energy densities are maximum at the mean position and zero at the extreme position. Hence, option 1 is incorrect.

Since the energy density is non-uniform at any given instant, all small parts of equal length do not possess equal energies in a travelling wave. Hence, option 3 is incorrect.

In a standing wave, energy is confined within regions and no net energy is transmitted along the string. Each small part of the string executes simple harmonic motion with a fixed amplitude depending on its position.

For a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the total energy is constant. Therefore, the energy of any small part of the string remains constant in a standing wave. Hence, option 2 is correct.

In a standing wave, the amplitude of oscillation varies with position, being zero at the nodes and maximum at the antinodes. Since the total energy of an oscillator depends on the square of its amplitude, small parts of equal length located at different positions will have different energies. Hence, option 4 is incorrect.

304987.subject: Physics
304987.text: The total work performed on a particle is equal to the change in its kinetic energy
options: only if gravitational force alone acts on it
only if the forces acting on it are conservative
only if elastic force alone acts on it
304987.sol:
According to the work-energy theorem, the total work done by all the forces acting on a particle is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.

$W_{\text{net}} = \Delta K$

This theorem is valid for all types of forces, including conservative, non-conservative, internal, and external forces. Therefore, it holds true in all cases.

305297.subject: Physics
305297.text: Through resistanceless leads, a capacitor of capacitance $12.0 \mu\text{F}$ is connected to a battery of emf $6.00 \text{ V}$ and internal resistance $1.00 \Omega$. Determine the power delivered by the battery $12.0 \mu\text{s}$ after the connections are made.
305297.sol:
The time constant of the RC circuit is given by:

$\tau = RC = 1.00 \times 12.0 \times 10^{-6} = 12.0 \mu\text{s}$

The current in the circuit as a function of time is:

$I(t) = \dfrac{E}{R} e^{-t/\tau}$

At $t = 12.0 \mu\text{s}$, we have $t = \tau$. Substituting the values:

$I = \dfrac{6.00}{1.00} e^{-1} = \dfrac{6.00}{e} \approx 2.207 \text{ A}$

The total power delivered by the battery is the power supplied by its emf, which is given by:

$P = EI$

$P = 6.00 \times 2.207 \approx 13.24 \text{ W}$

Rounding to three significant figures, the power delivered is $13.2 \text{ W}$.

305564.subject: Physics
305564.text: A coil with a resistance of $40 \Omega$ is connected across a $4.0 \text{ V}$ battery. If the current in the coil is $63 \text{ mA}$ exactly $0.10 \text{ s}$ after making the connection, determine the inductance of the coil.
305564.sol:
The growth of current in an LR circuit is given by the equation:

$I = I_{0}(1 - e^{-Rt/L})$

The steady state maximum current $I_{0}$ is:

$I_{0} = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{4.0}{40} = 0.1 \text{ A} = 100 \text{ mA}$

Given that the current $I = 63 \text{ mA}$ at time $t = 0.10 \text{ s}$, substituting these values into the equation gives:

$63 = 100(1 - e^{-40 \times 0.10 / L})$

$0.63 = 1 - e^{-4.0/L}$

$e^{-4.0/L} = 1 - 0.63 = 0.37$

Since $e^{-1} \approx 0.37$, equating the exponents gives:

$\dfrac{4.0}{L} = 1$

$L = 4.0 \text{ H}$

306022.subject: Physics
306022.text: A long bar magnet possesses a pole strength of $10 \text{ Am}$. Determine the magnetic field at a point situated on the magnet's axis, at a distance of $5 \text{ cm}$ from its north pole.
306022.sol:
Since the bar magnet is long, the magnetic field at a point near one of its poles is effectively due to that pole alone. The contribution from the other pole is negligible.

The magnetic field $B$ at a distance $r$ from a magnetic pole of strength $m$ is given by:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{m}{r^2}$

Given $m = 10 \text{ Am}$ and $r = 5 \text{ cm} = 0.05 \text{ m}$.

Substituting the values:

$B = 10^{-7} \times \dfrac{10}{(0.05)^2}$

$B = 10^{-7} \times \dfrac{10}{25 \times 10^{-4}}$

$B = 10^{-7} \times 4000$

$B = 4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ T}$

306063.subject: Physics
306063.text: A photoelectric material has a work function of $4.0 \text{ eV}$. Determine its threshold wavelength.
306063.sol:
The work function $\Phi$ and threshold wavelength $\lambda_0$ are related by the equation:

$\Phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0}$

Given $\Phi = 4.0 \text{ eV}$ and using the standard value $hc \approx 1240 \text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}$, we get:

$\lambda_0 = \dfrac{1240 \text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}}{4.0 \text{ eV}}$

$\lambda_0 = 310 \text{ nm}$

306190.subject: Physics
306190.text: Two rigid vessels $A$ and $B$, each having a volume of $200 \text{ cm}^3$, contain an ideal gas ($C_V = 12.5 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$). These vessels are connected to a manometer tube containing mercury. Initially, the pressure in both vessels is $75 \text{ cm}$ of mercury and the temperature is $300 \text{ K}$. Subsequently, $5.0 \text{ J}$ of heat is supplied to the gas in vessel $A$ and $10 \text{ J}$ to the gas in vessel $B$. Assuming no appreciable transfer of heat from $A$ to $B$, calculate the difference in the heights of mercury in the two sides of the manometer. Take the gas constant $R = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
306190.sol:
For a constant volume process, the heat supplied is $Q = n C_V \Delta T$.

From the ideal gas equation $PV = nRT$, the change in pressure at constant volume is $\Delta P = \dfrac{n R \Delta T}{V}$.

Substituting $n \Delta T = \dfrac{Q}{C_V}$, we get $\Delta P = \dfrac{R Q}{V C_V}$.

The difference in pressure between vessel B and vessel A is:
$\Delta P_{net} = \Delta P_B - \Delta P_A = \dfrac{R}{V C_V} (Q_B - Q_A)$

Substituting the given values ($R = 8.3 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, $V = 200 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3$, $C_V = 12.5 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$, $Q_B - Q_A = 5.0 \text{ J}$):
$\Delta P_{net} = \dfrac{8.3 \times 5.0}{2 \times 10^{-4} \times 12.5} = 16600 \text{ N m}^{-2}$

To convert this pressure difference into cm of Hg, we use $\rho_{Hg} = 13600 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $g = 9.8 \text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$1 \text{ cm of Hg} = 0.01 \times 13600 \times 9.8 = 1332.8 \text{ N m}^{-2}$

The difference in height $h$ is:
$h = \dfrac{16600}{1332.8} \approx 12.45 \text{ cm}$

This value is approximately $12.5 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: $12.5 \text{ cm}$

306193.text: An adiabatic cylindrical tube having a volume $V_0$ is separated into two parts by a frictionless adiabatic separator, as shown in the figure. Initially, the separator is held in the middle. The left part is filled with an ideal gas at pressure $p_1$ and temperature $T_1$, while the right part contains another ideal gas at pressure $p_2$ and temperature $T_2$. The specific heat ratio, $C_p / C_V = \gamma$, is identical for both gases. The separator is subsequently slid slowly and released at a location where it can remain in equilibrium. Determine the final volumes of the left and right parts respectively.
306193.sol:
Since the separator is adiabatic and the process is slow, the expansion or compression of both gases is reversible and adiabatic.

For an adiabatic process, $pV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$.

Let the final pressure of both gases in equilibrium be $p$. The initial volume of each part is $\dfrac{V_0}{2}$.

For the left part:
$p_1 \left(\dfrac{V_0}{2}\right)^{\gamma} = p V_1^{\gamma} \Rightarrow V_1 = \dfrac{V_0}{2} \left(\dfrac{p_1}{p}\right)^{1/\gamma}$

For the right part:
$p_2 \left(\dfrac{V_0}{2}\right)^{\gamma} = p V_2^{\gamma} \Rightarrow V_2 = \dfrac{V_0}{2} \left(\dfrac{p_2}{p}\right)^{1/\gamma}$

The total volume of the tube remains constant, so $V_1 + V_2 = V_0$.

Substituting the expressions for $V_1$ and $V_2$:
$\dfrac{V_0}{2} \left(\dfrac{p_1}{p}\right)^{1/\gamma} + \dfrac{V_0}{2} \left(\dfrac{p_2}{p}\right)^{1/\gamma} = V_0$

$\dfrac{1}{2 p^{1/\gamma}} \left( p_1^{1/\gamma} + p_2^{1/\gamma} \right) = 1$

\left(\dfrac{1}{p}\right)^{1/\gamma} = \dfrac{2}{p_1^{1/\gamma} + p_2^{1/\gamma}}$

Substituting this back into the equations for $V_1$ and $V_2$:

$V_1 = \dfrac{V_0}{2} p_1^{1/\gamma} \left( \dfrac{2}{p_1^{1/\gamma} + p_2^{1/\gamma}} \right) = \dfrac{p_1^{1/\gamma} V_0}{p_1^{1/\gamma} + p_2^{1/\gamma}}$

$V_2 = \dfrac{V_0}{2} p_2^{1/\gamma} \left( \dfrac{2}{p_1^{1/\gamma} + p_2^{1/\gamma}} \right) = \dfrac{p_2^{1/\gamma} V_0}{p_1^{1/\gamma} + p_2^{1/\gamma}}

306511.text: For a gas at absolute temperature $T$, the mean square speed of its molecules is proportional to
306511.sol:
The mean square speed of gas molecules is given by the square of the root mean square speed.

The root mean square speed is $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

Squaring both sides, the mean square speed is $v_{rms}^2 = \dfrac{3RT}{M}$

Alternatively, from the kinetic theory of gases, the average translational kinetic energy of a molecule is $\dfrac{1}{2} m \overline{v^2} = \dfrac{3}{2} k_B T$

This gives $\overline{v^2} = \dfrac{3 k_B T}{m}$

Therefore, the mean square speed is directly proportional to the absolute temperature $T$.

306562.subject: Physics
306562.text: Negative magnetic susceptibility is exhibited by
306562.sol:
Magnetic susceptibility $\chi$ is defined as the ratio of the intensity of magnetization $M$ to the magnetic intensity $H$.

For diamagnetic materials, the induced magnetization is in the direction opposite to the applied magnetic field. Therefore, they have a small and negative magnetic susceptibility ($-1 \le \chi < 0$).

For paramagnetic materials, the susceptibility is small and positive ($\chi > 0$).

For ferromagnetic materials, the susceptibility is large and positive ($\chi \gg 1$).

Thus, negative magnetic susceptibility is exhibited by diamagnetic materials only.

306710.subject: Physics
306710.text: As one travels along the $x$-axis from $x = -1 \text{ cm}$ to $x = +1 \text{ cm}$, the electric potential decreases uniformly from $120 \text{ V}$ to $80 \text{ V}$. Which of the following is true regarding the electric field at the origin?
options: It must be equal to $20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$
It may be less than $20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$
It may be equal to $20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$
It may be greater than $20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$
306710.sol:
The $x$-component of the electric field is given by $E_{x} = -\dfrac{\partial V}{\partial x}$.

Since the potential decreases uniformly along the $x$-axis, we have $E_{x} = -\dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta x} = -\dfrac{80 - 120}{1 - (-1)} = 20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$.

The total electric field is $\vec{E} = E_{x} \hat{i} + E_{y} \hat{j} + E_{z} \hat{k}$.

The magnitude of the electric field is $E = \sqrt{E_{x}^2 + E_{y}^2 + E_{z}^2} = \sqrt{20^2 + E_{y}^2 + E_{z}^2}$.

Since the variation of potential along the $y$ and $z$ axes is not given, $E_{y}$ and $E_{z}$ are unknown and can be zero or non-zero.

Therefore, $E \ge 20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$.

Thus, the magnitude of the electric field may be equal to $20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$ (if $E_{y} = E_{z} = 0$) or it may be greater than $20 \text{ V cm}^{-1}$ (if $E_{y} \ne 0$ or $E_{z} \ne 0$).

309241.subject: Chemistry
309241.text:
Identify the major product of the following reaction sequence:



(i) $\mathrm{LDA}$
(ii) $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}$
(iii) $\mathrm{NaBH}_4$ / $\mathrm{MeOH}$
309241.sol:
The given starting material is cyclopentanone.

Step (i): Reaction with $\mathrm{LDA}$ (Lithium diisopropylamide), which is a strong, bulky base. It abstracts an $\alpha$-proton from cyclopentanone to form a lithium enolate.

Step (ii): Reaction with $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}$ (Methyl iodide). The enolate acts as a nucleophile and undergoes an $S_N2$ reaction with $\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{I}$, resulting in the $\alpha$-alkylation of the ketone to form 2-methylcyclopentanone.

Step (iii): Reaction with $\mathrm{NaBH}_4$ in $\mathrm{MeOH}$. Sodium borohydride is a reducing agent that reduces the ketone carbonyl group to a secondary alcohol. Thus, 2-methylcyclopentanone is reduced to 2-methylcyclopentanol.

Comparing this with the given options, the final major product is 2-methylcyclopentanol.

Answer:

309385.subject: Chemistry
309385.text:
The cyclic hemiacetal shown below is in equilibrium with an acyclic open-chain compound $\mathrm{X}$ in aqueous solution.


Identify the structure of compound $\mathrm{X}$.
309385.sol:
The given compound is a six-membered cyclic hemiacetal.

In aqueous solution, it undergoes ring opening to form an acyclic aldehyde.

The anomeric carbon ($\text{C}_1$), which is bonded to both the ring oxygen and a hydroxyl group, becomes the aldehyde carbonyl carbon ($-\text{CHO}$) upon ring opening.

The ring oxygen is attached to $\text{C}_5$ of the chain. When the $\text{C}_1-\text{O}$ bond breaks, this oxygen becomes a hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) on $\text{C}_5$.

The substituent on $\text{C}_5$ is a $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group, which constitutes $\text{C}_6$.

Therefore, the open-chain form has a six-carbon skeleton with an aldehyde at $\text{C}_1$ and hydroxyl groups at $\text{C}_5$ and $\text{C}_6$.

The structure is $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$ (5,6-dihydroxyhexanal).

Option (A) correctly shows this 5,6-dihydroxyhexanal structure.

Options (B), (C), and (D) represent a ketone, a triol, and a carboxylic acid, respectively, which cannot form the given hemiacetal.

Answer:

314746.text: $a, b, c$ are positive real numbers such that $a^2+b^2 =c^2$ and $a b=c$. Determine the value of $\left|\frac{(a+b+c)(a+b-c)(b+c-a)(c+a-b)}{c^2}\right|$.
314746.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& a^2+b^2=c^2, a b=c \\
& (a+b)^2=a^2+b^2+2 a b=c^2+2 c \\
& (a+b)^2-c^2=2 c ...(i)\\
& (a-b)^2=c^2-2 c \Rightarrow c^2-(a-b)^2=2 c ...(ii)
\end{aligned}$

Given expression is
$\frac{\left((a+b)^2-c^2\right)\left(c^2-(a-b)^2\right)}{c^2}=\frac{2 c \times 2 c}{c^2}=4$

6a13e465688ac6d0667aad06.text: A student constructs a circuit using three capacitors as shown in the given figure. What will be the effective capacitance between the terminals X and Y?
6a13e465688ac6d0667aad06.sol:
In the given circuit, the $3\ \mu\text{F}$ and $6\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitors are connected in series. Their equivalent capacitance $C_s$ is:

$C_s = \dfrac{3 \times 6}{3 + 6} = \dfrac{18}{9} = 2\ \mu\text{F}$

This combination is connected in parallel with the $2\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor.

The effective capacitance $C_{XY}$ between terminals X and Y is:

$C_{XY} = 2\ \mu\text{F} + C_s$

$C_{XY} = 2\ \mu\text{F} + 2\ \mu\text{F} = 4\ \mu\text{F}$

Answer: $4\ \mu\text{F}$

6a2a77bffad2360f42564beb.subject: Biology
6a2a77bffad2360f42564beb.text:
Read the following statements regarding the enzymes used in recombinant DNA technology and identify the incorrect statements.
A. Exonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.
B. A restriction endonuclease inspects the length of a DNA sequence to find its specific recognition sequence.
C. EcoRI cuts the DNA between bases G and A only when the sequence GAATTC is present in the DNA.
D. DNA ligase joins the two DNA molecules by forming hydrogen bonds between the sticky ends.
E. The first restriction endonuclease whose functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence was Hind II.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6a2a77bffad2360f42564beb.sol:
Statement A is incorrect because exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of the DNA, whereas endonucleases make cuts at specific positions within the DNA.

Statement B is correct as each restriction endonuclease functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence to find its specific recognition sequence.

Statement C is correct because EcoRI specifically recognizes the palindromic sequence GAATTC and cuts the DNA between the bases G and A.

Statement D is incorrect because DNA ligase joins two DNA molecules by forming phosphodiester bonds between adjacent nucleotides of the sugar-phosphate backbone, not by forming hydrogen bonds. Hydrogen bonds between sticky ends form spontaneously due to complementary base pairing.

Statement E is correct as Hind II was the first restriction endonuclease to be discovered and its functioning depended on a specific DNA nucleotide sequence.

Therefore, the incorrect statements are A and D.

Answer: A and D only

6a7a1ff82f4492ea8706705a.text: A solid sphere attains a constant terminal velocity while falling through a viscous liquid. It is observed that the viscous drag force acting on the sphere is $k$ times the buoyant force exerted by the liquid. The ratio of the density of the sphere's material to the density of the liquid is:
6a7a1ff82f4492ea8706705a.sol:
Let the volume of the sphere be $V$, the density of the sphere's material be $\rho$, and the density of the liquid be $\rho_l$.

The weight of the sphere is $W = \rho V g$.
The buoyant force is $B = \rho_l V g$.

At constant terminal velocity, the net force on the sphere is zero. Therefore, the downward weight is balanced by the upward buoyant force and the viscous drag force $F_v$.
$W = B + F_v$

It is given that $F_v = k B$. Substituting this into the force balance equation gives:
$W = B + k B = B(k+1)$

Substituting the expressions for $W$ and $B$:
$\rho V g = \rho_l V g (k+1)$

Dividing both sides by $V g$ yields:
$\rho = \rho_l (k+1)$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\rho}{\rho_l} = k+1$

Answer: $k+1$

6a7a1ff8c2e30fc0b7fb5a48.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8c2e30fc0b7fb5a48.text: A gaseous mixture is prepared by mixing $n$ moles of a monatomic gas and $2n$ moles of a rigid diatomic gas. The ratio of specific heats at constant pressure to that at constant volume for this mixture is:
6a7a1ff8c2e30fc0b7fb5a48.sol:
For a monatomic gas, the number of degrees of freedom is $f_1 = 3$.
For a rigid diatomic gas, the number of degrees of freedom is $f_2 = 5$.

The effective number of degrees of freedom for a mixture of $n_1$ moles of gas 1 and $n_2$ moles of gas 2 is given by:

$f_{mix} = \dfrac{n_1 f_1 + n_2 f_2}{n_1 + n_2}$

Substituting the given values ($n_1 = n$ and $n_2 = 2n$):

$f_{mix} = \dfrac{n(3) + 2n(5)}{n + 2n} = \dfrac{3n + 10n}{3n} = \dfrac{13}{3}$

The ratio of specific heats for the mixture $\gamma_{mix}$ is:

$\gamma_{mix} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f_{mix}} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{\left(\dfrac{13}{3}\right)} = 1 + \dfrac{6}{13} = \dfrac{19}{13}$

Answer: $\dfrac{19}{13}$

6a7a1ff83ddf742321a1408b.text: The equation of a progressive transverse wave is given by $y = A \sin(\omega t - kx)$. If the maximum speed of a particle in the medium is equal to $4$ times the wave propagation speed, then the wavelength of the wave is:
6a7a1ff83ddf742321a1408b.sol:
The maximum velocity of a particle in the medium is $v_{p,\text{max}} = A\omega$.

The wave propagation speed is $v_w = \dfrac{\omega}{k}$.

We know that the wave number $k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}$, so $v_w = \dfrac{\omega \lambda}{2\pi}$.

According to the given condition, $v_{p,\text{max}} = 4 v_w$.

Substituting the expressions, we get:
$A\omega = 4 \left(\dfrac{\omega \lambda}{2\pi}\right)$

$A = \dfrac{2\lambda}{\pi}$

Rearranging for wavelength $\lambda$, we obtain $\lambda = \dfrac{\pi A}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi A}{2}$

6a7a1ff819cb6cf1ac72be54.text: A Young's double slit experiment is first performed in air using light of wavelength $500\text{ nm}$. The slit separation is $2.0\text{ mm}$ and the screen is placed at a distance of $1.2\text{ m}$ from the slits. The entire setup is then immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.25$. What is the minimum non-zero distance from the central maximum where a bright fringe of the interference pattern in air would exactly coincide with a dark fringe of the interference pattern in the liquid?
6a7a1ff819cb6cf1ac72be54.sol:
The position of the $n^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe in air is given by:
$y_1 = n \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$

When immersed in the liquid, the wavelength becomes $\dfrac{\lambda}{\mu}$. The position of the $m^{\text{th}}$ dark fringe in the liquid is given by:
$y_2 = (m - 0.5) \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d}$

For the fringes to coincide, $y_1 = y_2$:
$n \dfrac{\lambda D}{d} = (m - 0.5) \dfrac{\lambda D}{\mu d}$

Simplifying, we get:
$n = \dfrac{m - 0.5}{\mu}$

Substitute $\mu = 1.25 = \dfrac{5}{4}$:
$n = \dfrac{4(m - 0.5)}{5}$
$\Rightarrow 5n = 4m - 2$

We need the smallest positive integers $n$ and $m$ that satisfy this equation.
Testing values for $m$ ($m = 1, 2, 3, \dots$):
If $m = 1$, $5n = 2$ (no integer solution)
If $m = 2$, $5n = 6$ (no integer solution)
If $m = 3$, $5n = 10 \Rightarrow n = 2$

The first coincidence occurs for the $2^{\text{nd}}$ bright fringe in air.
The distance from the central maximum is:
$y = 2 \times \dfrac{500 \times 10^{-9} \times 1.2}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}}$
$y = \dfrac{1200 \times 10^{-9}}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}} = 600 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m} = 0.60\text{ mm}$.

Answer: $0.60\text{ mm}$

6a7a1ff8ffa4cde28695dd31.text: The least count of a vernier caliper is $y$. The length of one main scale division is $x$. If $N$ divisions of the vernier scale coincide with $M$ divisions of the main scale, then the value of $N$ is given by:
6a7a1ff8ffa4cde28695dd31.sol:
The least count (L.C.) of a vernier caliper is given by the difference between one main scale division (MSD) and one vernier scale division (VSD).

Given that $1 \text{ MSD} = x$ and $\text{L.C.} = y$.

Since $N$ divisions of the vernier scale coincide with $M$ divisions of the main scale, we have:
$N \text{ VSD} = M \text{ MSD}$
$\Rightarrow 1 \text{ VSD} = \dfrac{M}{N} \text{ MSD} = \dfrac{M}{N} x$

Now, substitute this into the least count formula:
$\text{L.C.} = 1 \text{ MSD} - 1 \text{ VSD}$
$y = x - \dfrac{M}{N} x$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $N$:
$\dfrac{M}{N} x = x - y$
$\dfrac{M}{N} = \dfrac{x - y}{x}$
$N = \dfrac{Mx}{x - y}$

Answer: $\dfrac{Mx}{x-y}$

6a7a1ff83b29a1de4f372c54.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff83b29a1de4f372c54.text:
Solid manganese dioxide reacts with aqueous hydrochloric acid to form manganese(II) chloride, water, and chlorine gas. If $261\text{ g}$ of $\text{MnO}_2$ is reacted with $292\text{ g}$ of $\text{HCl}$, the volume of chlorine gas produced at STP is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ L}$. The value of $x$ is ____.

(Given: Molar masses in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Mn} = 55$, $\text{O} = 16$, $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{Cl} = 35.5$. Molar volume of gas at STP $= 22.7\text{ L}$)
6a7a1ff83b29a1de4f372c54.sol:
The balanced chemical equation for the reaction is:
$\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{MnCl}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2$

First, calculate the number of moles of each reactant.
Molar mass of $\text{MnO}_2 = 55 + (2 \times 16) = 87\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of $\text{MnO}_2 = \dfrac{261}{87} = 3\text{ mol}$

Molar mass of $\text{HCl} = 1 + 35.5 = 36.5\text{ g mol}^{-1}$
Moles of $\text{HCl} = \dfrac{292}{36.5} = 8\text{ mol}$

From the balanced equation, $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{MnO}_2$ requires $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$.
So, $3\text{ mol}$ of $\text{MnO}_2$ would require $12\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$.
Since only $8\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$ is available, $\text{HCl}$ is the limiting reagent.

The amount of $\text{Cl}_2$ produced depends on the limiting reagent ($\text{HCl}$).
From the equation, $4\text{ mol}$ of $\text{HCl}$ produces $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Cl}_2$.
Moles of $\text{Cl}_2$ produced $= \dfrac{1}{4} \times 8 = 2\text{ mol}$

Volume of $\text{Cl}_2$ at STP $= \text{Moles} \times \text{Molar volume}$
Volume $= 2 \times 22.7 = 45.4\text{ L}$

We are given that the volume is $x \times 10^{-1}\text{ L}$.
Therefore, $45.4 = x \times 10^{-1} \implies x = 454$.

Answer: $454$

6a7a1ff86fde4a35e0f5034d.text: Among the alkali metals $\text{Li}, \text{Na}, \text{K}, \text{Rb}$, and $\text{Cs}$, the number of metals that form predominantly a superoxide upon heating in excess air AND have a density less than $1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ is
6a7a1ff86fde4a35e0f5034d.sol:
Alkali metals that form predominantly superoxides when heated in excess air are $\text{K}, \text{Rb}$, and $\text{Cs}$.

The densities of the given alkali metals are approximately:
$\text{Li} = 0.53 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{Na} = 0.97 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{K} = 0.86 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{Rb} = 1.53 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$
$\text{Cs} = 1.90 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$

The metals with a density less than $1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ are $\text{Li}, \text{Na}$, and $\text{K}$.

The only metal satisfying both conditions (forming a superoxide and having density $< 1.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$) is $\text{K}$.

Therefore, the number of such metals is $1$.

Answer: $1$

6a7a1ff83f56a0bba1b6df7d.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff83f56a0bba1b6df7d.text: An unknown gaseous compound X is prepared by treating $NaBH_4$ with $I_2$. Compound X reacts with excess ammonia at low temperature to form an ionic adduct Y. Upon heating, compound Y decomposes to give a cyclic compound Z. Identify the correct statement regarding X, Y, or Z.
options: Compound X undergoes symmetrical cleavage upon reaction with ammonia to form Y.
The cationic part of compound Y contains an $sp^2$ hybridized boron atom.
Compound Z is an aromatic-like cyclic compound known as inorganic benzene.
In compound X, all the $B-H$ bonds are of equal length.
6a7a1ff83f56a0bba1b6df7d.sol:
The reaction of sodium borohydride with iodine produces diborane (X):
$2NaBH_4 + I_2 \rightarrow B_2H_6 + 2NaI + H_2$

Diborane (X) reacts with ammonia at low temperature to undergo unsymmetrical cleavage, forming the ionic adduct Y:
$B_2H_6 + 2NH_3 \rightarrow [BH_2(NH_3)_2]^+[BH_4]^-$

Upon heating, the ionic adduct Y forms borazine (Z):
$3[BH_2(NH_3)_2]^+[BH_4]^- \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2B_3N_3H_6 + 12H_2$

Evaluating the given options:
- Compound X ($B_2H_6$) undergoes unsymmetrical cleavage with $NH_3$, not symmetrical.
- The cationic part of Y is $[BH_2(NH_3)_2]^+$, where the boron atom forms four sigma bonds and is $sp^3$ hybridized, not $sp^2$.
- Compound Z ($B_3N_3H_6$) is borazine, which is structurally similar to benzene and is known as inorganic benzene.
- In compound X ($B_2H_6$), the terminal $B-H$ bonds are shorter than the bridging $B-H$ bonds, so they are not of equal length.
Therefore, the correct statement is that Z is an aromatic-like cyclic compound known as inorganic benzene.

Answer: Compound Z is an aromatic-like cyclic compound known as inorganic benzene.

6a7a1ff8d4ca3ad567dda79f.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff8d4ca3ad567dda79f.text:
Complete combustion of $0.50 \text{ g}$ of an oxygen-containing organic compound gave $0.88 \text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $0.90 \text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The percentage of oxygen in the compound is _______.

[Given : Molar mass (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) $\text{C}: 12, \text{H}: 1, \text{O}: 16$]
6a7a1ff8d4ca3ad567dda79f.sol:
Mass of carbon in the compound $= \dfrac{12}{44} \times \text{Mass of CO}_2 = \dfrac{12}{44} \times 0.88 = 0.24 \text{ g}$

Mass of hydrogen in the compound $= \dfrac{2}{18} \times \text{Mass of H}_2\text{O} = \dfrac{2}{18} \times 0.90 = 0.10 \text{ g}$

Total mass of carbon and hydrogen $= 0.24 + 0.10 = 0.34 \text{ g}$

Since the compound contains only carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen, the mass of oxygen is:
Mass of oxygen $= \text{Total mass of compound} - (\text{Mass of C} + \text{Mass of H}) = 0.50 - 0.34 = 0.16 \text{ g}$

Percentage of oxygen $= \dfrac{0.16}{0.50} \times 100 = 32\%$

Answer: $32$

6a7a1ff8e207ff3adf600ea5.text: An aqueous solution of a solute (molar mass $= 150\text{ g/mol}$) has a density of $1.4\text{ g/mL}$. If the ratio of its molarity to its molality is $0.8$, what is the molarity of the solution?
6a7a1ff8e207ff3adf600ea5.sol:
Let the molarity be $M$ and the molality be $m$.
Given that $\dfrac{M}{m} = 0.8$, we have $m = \dfrac{M}{0.8} = 1.25 M$.

The relationship between molality ($m$), molarity ($M$), density ($d$ in g/mL), and molar mass of solute ($M_w$ in g/mol) is:
$m = \dfrac{1000 \times M}{1000 \times d - M \times M_w}$

Substitute the given values ($d = 1.4\text{ g/mL}$, $M_w = 150\text{ g/mol}$, and $m = 1.25 M$):
$1.25 M = \dfrac{1000 M}{1000 \times 1.4 - M \times 150}$

Assuming $M \neq 0$, we can divide both sides by $M$:
$1.25 = \dfrac{1000}{1400 - 150 M}$

$1400 - 150 M = \dfrac{1000}{1.25}$

$1400 - 150 M = 800$

$150 M = 600$

$M = 4\text{ M}$.

Answer: $4\text{ M}$

6a7a1ff8c73a32f413d00be4.text: An acidified solution of potassium permanganate is treated with an excess of oxalic acid. The spin-only magnetic moment of the manganese-containing product formed in this reaction is closest to:
6a7a1ff8c73a32f413d00be4.sol:
In an acidic medium, potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$) oxidises oxalic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4$) to carbon dioxide and is itself reduced to the manganese(II) ion ($\text{Mn}^{2+}$).

The reaction is:
$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 + 6\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 10\text{CO}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The manganese-containing product is $\text{Mn}^{2+}$. The atomic number of Mn is 25, so its ground state electronic configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^5 4\text{s}^2$.

For the $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ion, the configuration is $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^5$. This gives $n = 5$ unpaired electrons.

The spin-only magnetic moment $\mu$ is calculated as:
$\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} \text{ BM} = \sqrt{5(5+2)} \text{ BM} = \sqrt{35} \text{ BM} \approx 5.92 \text{ BM}$

Answer: $5.92 \text{ BM}$

6a7a1ff86f056e3b06e12fc9.text: Consider the polynomial $P(x) = \left(x + \sqrt{x^2-k}\right)^5 + \left(x - \sqrt{x^2-k}\right)^5$, where $k$ is a positive constant. If the coefficient of $x^3$ in the simplified expansion of $P(x)$ is $-120$, then the coefficient of $x$ in $P(x)$ is :
6a7a1ff86f056e3b06e12fc9.sol:
Using the binomial expansion for $(a+b)^n + (a-b)^n$, we know that the terms with odd powers of $b$ cancel out.

$(a+b)^5 + (a-b)^5 = 2 \left[ ^{5}C_{0} a^5 + ^{5}C_{2} a^3 b^2 + ^{5}C_{4} a b^4 \right]$

Substitute $a = x$ and $b = \sqrt{x^2-k}$ :

$P(x) = 2 \left[ x^5 + 10 x^3 (x^2-k) + 5 x (x^2-k)^2 \right]$

Expanding the terms inside the bracket:

$P(x) = 2 \left[ x^5 + 10x^5 - 10kx^3 + 5x(x^4 - 2kx^2 + k^2) \right]$

$P(x) = 2 \left[ 11x^5 - 10kx^3 + 5x^5 - 10kx^3 + 5k^2x \right]$

6a7a1ff8e65958127b6788cb.text: The angle of elevation of a stationary hot air balloon from a point $P$ on the level ground is $45^\circ$. An observer moves a distance $d$ meters from $P$ towards the balloon along a straight path inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal ground. At the new position, the angle of elevation of the balloon is $60^\circ$. If the height of the balloon from the ground is $50(\sqrt{3}+1)$ meters, then the value of $d$ is :
6a7a1ff8e65958127b6788cb.sol:
Let the initial position of the observer be $P(0,0)$ and the balloon be at a height $h$.

Since the angle of elevation from $P$ is $45^\circ$, the horizontal distance to the balloon is also $h$.

So, the coordinates of the balloon are $(h, h)$, where $h = 50(\sqrt{3}+1)$.

The observer moves a distance $d$ along a path inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal.

The new position $Q$ has coordinates $\left(d \cos 30^\circ, d \sin 30^\circ\right) = \left(\dfrac{d\sqrt{3}}{2}, \dfrac{d}{2}\right)$.

From $Q$, the angle of elevation of the balloon is $60^\circ$.

The horizontal distance from $Q$ to the balloon is $h - \dfrac{d\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

The vertical distance from $Q$ to the balloon is $h - \dfrac{d}{2}$.

Thus, $\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{h - \dfrac{d}{2}}{h - \dfrac{d\sqrt{3}}{2}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{2h - d}{2h - d\sqrt{3}}$.

$2h\sqrt{3} - 3d = 2h - d \Rightarrow 2d = 2h(\sqrt{3} - 1) \Rightarrow d = h(\sqrt{3} - 1)$.

Substitute $h = 50(\sqrt{3}+1)$:

$d = 50(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1) = 50(3 - 1) = 100$ m.

Answer: $100$

6a7a1ff8cb9b2ffe12ebe796.text:
The number of values of $\theta \in (0, 3\pi)$ for which the system of linear equations

$x \cos 3\theta + y \cos 2\theta + z = 0$

$x + y + z = 0$

$2x + 3y + 4z = 0$

has non-trivial solutions is
6a7a1ff8cb9b2ffe12ebe796.sol:
For a homogeneous system of linear equations to have non-trivial solutions, the determinant of the coefficient matrix must be zero.



$D = \begin{vmatrix} \cos 3\theta & \cos 2\theta & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 0$



Expanding along the first row:



$\cos 3\theta (4 - 3) - \cos 2\theta (4 - 2) + 1 (3 - 2) = 0$



$\Rightarrow \cos 3\theta - 2\cos 2\theta + 1 = 0$



Using multiple angle identities $\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$ and $\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$:



$\Rightarrow (4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta) - 2(2\cos^2\theta - 1) + 1 = 0$



$\Rightarrow 4\cos^3\theta - 4\cos^2\theta - 3\cos\theta + 3 = 0$



$\Rightarrow 4\cos^2\theta(\cos\theta - 1) - 3(\cos\theta - 1) = 0$



$\Rightarrow (\cos\theta - 1)(4\cos^2\theta - 3) = 0$



This gives $\cos\theta = 1$ or $\cos\theta = \pm \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.



We need to find the number of solutions in the interval $(0, 3\pi)$.



For $\cos\theta = 1$: $\theta = 2\pi$ (1 solution)



For $\cos\theta = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$: $\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{6}, \dfrac{11\pi}{6}, \dfrac{13\pi}{6}$ (3 solutions)



For $\cos\theta = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$: $\theta = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}, \dfrac{7\pi}{6}, \dfrac{17\pi}{6}$ (3 solutions)



Total number of solutions = $1 + 3 + 3 = 7$.



Answer: $7$

6a7a1ff8b969a8baa96f9f48.text: Let $J = \int_{-3}^{3} \dfrac{9 - x^2}{(9 + x^2)\sqrt{81 + x^4}} \dfrac{1}{1 + 5^x} dx$. The value of $\dfrac{24\sqrt{2}}{\pi} J$ is equal to ______.
6a7a1ff8b969a8baa96f9f48.sol:
Using the property $\int_{-a}^{a} \dfrac{f(x)}{1+c^x} dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(x) dx$ for an even function $f(x)$, we have:

$J = \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{9 - x^2}{(9 + x^2)\sqrt{81 + x^4}} dx$

Dividing the numerator and denominator by $x^2$:

$J = \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{\dfrac{9}{x^2} - 1}{\left(x + \dfrac{9}{x}\right)\sqrt{x^2 + \dfrac{81}{x^2}}} dx$

$J = \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{\dfrac{9}{x^2} - 1}{\left(x + \dfrac{9}{x}\right)\sqrt{\left(x + \dfrac{9}{x}\right)^2 - 18}} dx$

Let $t = x + \dfrac{9}{x}$. Then $dt = \left(1 - \dfrac{9}{x^2}\right) dx \Rightarrow \left(\dfrac{9}{x^2} - 1\right) dx = -dt$.

When $x \to 0$, $t \to \infty$. When $x = 3$, $t = 3 + 3 = 6$.

$J = \int_{\infty}^{6} \dfrac{-dt}{t\sqrt{t^2 - 18}} = \int_{6}^{\infty} \dfrac{dt}{t\sqrt{t^2 - 18}}$

Using the standard integral $\int \dfrac{dx}{x\sqrt{x^2 - a^2}} = \dfrac{1}{a} \sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right) + C$:

$J = \left[ \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{t}{3\sqrt{2}}\right) \right]_{6}^{\infty}$

$J = \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \left( \sec^{-1}(\infty) - \sec^{-1}\left(\dfrac{6}{3\sqrt{2}}\right) \right)$

$J = \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sec^{-1}(\sqrt{2}) \right) = \dfrac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \left( \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} \right) = \dfrac{\pi}{12\sqrt{2}}$

Therefore, $\dfrac{24\sqrt{2}}{\pi} J = \dfrac{24\sqrt{2}}{\pi} \times \dfrac{\pi}{12\sqrt{2}} = 2$.

Answer: $2$

6a7a1ff83d5a4349d83475c3.text: A quadratic polynomial $f(x)$ satisfies $f(0) = 3$, $f'(2) = 0$, and $f''(x) = 2$ for all $x$. If the area of the region bounded by $y = f(x)$ and $y = \min\{x - 1, 5 - 3x\}$ is $A$, then the value of $6A$ is
6a7a1ff83d5a4349d83475c3.sol:
First, we determine the quadratic polynomial $f(x)$.
Given $f''(x) = 2$, integrating yields $f'(x) = 2x + c_1$.
Using $f'(2) = 0$, we get $2(2) + c_1 = 0 \Rightarrow c_1 = -4$. Thus, $f'(x) = 2x - 4$.
Integrating again gives $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + c_2$.
Using $f(0) = 3$, we get $c_2 = 3$. Therefore, $f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3$.

Next, we find the area of the region bounded by $y = x^2 - 4x + 3$ and $y = \min\{x - 1, 5 - 3x\}$.
Find the intersection of the two lines inside the min function:
$x - 1 = 5 - 3x \Rightarrow 4x = 6 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{3}{2}$.
For $x \leq \dfrac{3}{2}$, $x - 1 \leq 5 - 3x$, so the upper boundary is $y = x - 1$.
For $x \geq \dfrac{3}{2}$, $5 - 3x \leq x - 1$, so the upper boundary is $y = 5 - 3x$.

Now, find the intersection points of $f(x)$ with these lines:
For $x \leq \dfrac{3}{2}$: $x^2 - 4x + 3 = x - 1 \Rightarrow x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 1)(x - 4) = 0$. The valid intersection is at $x = 1$.
For $x \geq \dfrac{3}{2}$: $x^2 - 4x + 3 = 5 - 3x \Rightarrow x^2 - x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow (x - 2)(x + 1) = 0$. The valid intersection is at $x = 2$.

The total area $A$ is the sum of two integrals:
$A = \int_1^{3/2} ((x - 1) - (x^2 - 4x + 3)) dx + \int_{3/2}^2 ((5 - 3x) - (x^2 - 4x + 3)) dx$
$A = \int_1^{3/2} (-x^2 + 5x - 4) dx + \int_{3/2}^2 (-x^2 + x + 2) dx$

Evaluating the first integral:
$\int_1^{3/2} (-x^2 + 5x - 4) dx = \left[ -\dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{5x^2}{2} - 4x \right]_1^{3/2} = \left( -\dfrac{9}{8} + \dfrac{45}{8} - 6 \right) - \left( -\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{5}{2} - 4 \right) = -\dfrac{3}{2} - \left( -\dfrac{11}{6} \right) = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Evaluating the second integral:
$\int_{3/2}^2 (-x^2 + x + 2) dx = \left[ -\dfrac{x^3}{3} + \dfrac{x^2}{2} + 2x \right]_{3/2}^2 = \left( -\dfrac{8}{3} + 2 + 4 \right) - \left( -\dfrac{9}{8} + \dfrac{9}{8} + 3 \right) = \dfrac{10}{3} - 3 = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Total area $A = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Therefore, $6A = 6 \times \dfrac{2}{3} = 4$.

Answer: 4

6a7a1ff8b29b7a266e344cd4.text: Let $I$ be the image of the point $P(2, 0, 1)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{1} = \dfrac{z-2}{3}$. If $O$ is the origin, then the square of the area of the parallelogram whose adjacent sides are represented by the vectors $\vec{OP}$ and $\vec{OI}$ is :
6a7a1ff8b29b7a266e344cd4.sol:
Let the given line be $\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{1} = \dfrac{z-2}{3} = \lambda$.

A general point $F$ on this line is $F(2\lambda + 1, \lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 2)$.
Assuming $F$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $P(2, 0, 1)$ to the line, the direction ratios of $PF$ are:
$\langle 2\lambda + 1 - 2, \lambda - 1 - 0, 3\lambda + 2 - 1 \rangle = \langle 2\lambda - 1, \lambda - 1, 3\lambda + 1 \rangle$

Since $PF$ is perpendicular to the line, the dot product of their direction ratios is zero:
$2(2\lambda - 1) + 1(\lambda - 1) + 3(3\lambda + 1) = 0$
$\Rightarrow 4\lambda - 2 + \lambda - 1 + 9\lambda + 3 = 0$
$\Rightarrow 14\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 0$

Thus, the foot of the perpendicular is $F(1, -1, 2)$.

Since $F$ is the midpoint of $P$ and its image $I(x, y, z)$, we have:
$I = 2F - P = (2(1) - 2, 2(-1) - 0, 2(2) - 1) = (0, -2, 3)$

The vectors representing the adjacent sides of the parallelogram are:
$\vec{OP} = 2\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + \hat{k}$
$\vec{OI} = 0\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$

The area of the parallelogram is given by $|\vec{OP} \times \vec{OI}|$.
$\vec{OP} \times \vec{OI} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -2 & 3 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(0 - (-2)) - \hat{j}(6 - 0) + \hat{k}(-4 - 0) = 2\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$

The square of the area is:
$|\vec{OP} \times \vec{OI}|^2 = (2)^2 + (-6)^2 + (-4)^2 = 4 + 36 + 16 = 56$

Answer: $56$

6a7a1ff86943932e22a700c0.text: A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $P(X=x) = c(x+1)\alpha^x$ for $x = 0, 1, 2, \dots$, where $c$ and $\alpha$ are positive constants. If $2P(X=1) = 3P(X=2)$, then the value of $P(X \ge 2)$ is equal to
6a7a1ff86943932e22a700c0.sol:
Given $2P(X=1) = 3P(X=2)$

$\Rightarrow 2[c(1+1)\alpha^1] = 3[c(2+1)\alpha^2]$

$\Rightarrow 4c\alpha = 9c\alpha^2$

Since $c$ and $\alpha$ are positive constants, $\alpha = \dfrac{4}{9}$.

The sum of all probabilities must be 1:

$\sum_{x=0}^{\infty} P(X=x) = 1$

$\Rightarrow c \sum_{x=0}^{\infty} (x+1)\alpha^x = 1$

The series is an arithmetico-geometric progression:

$S = 1 + 2\alpha + 3\alpha^2 + \dots = \dfrac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2}$

$\Rightarrow c \times \dfrac{1}{(1-\alpha)^2} = 1 \Rightarrow c = (1-\alpha)^2 = \left(1 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right)^2 = \dfrac{25}{81}$

We need to find $P(X \ge 2)$:

$P(X \ge 2) = 1 - P(X=0) - P(X=1)$

$P(X=0) = c(1)\alpha^0 = c = \dfrac{25}{81} = \dfrac{225}{729}$

$P(X=1) = c(2)\alpha^1 = 2 \times \dfrac{25}{81} \times \dfrac{4}{9} = \dfrac{200}{729}$

$P(X \ge 2) = 1 - \left(\dfrac{225}{729} + \dfrac{200}{729}\right) = 1 - \dfrac{425}{729} = \dfrac{304}{729}$

Answer: $\dfrac{304}{729}$
